anomalies.symptom: During the first minute of flight the vehicle was struck by two triggered lightning discharges (36.5 s and 52 s). Crew got master alarms, multiple caution/warning lights (three fuel-cell lights, AC bus light, fuel-cell disconnect, AC bus overload 1 and 2, Main Bus A and B out), a signal-conditioning-equipment (SCE) dropout that garbled telemetry, and loss/tumble of the inertial guidance platform.
anomalies.documented_cause: Vehicle-triggered lightning as it passed through electric fields (special report, ref. 12). First strike's induced transient on the battery-relay bus exceeded the current rate-of-change limit of the SCRs in the fuel-cell overload sensors, disconnecting the fuel cells from the main buses; low bus voltage dropped out the SCE and tripped AC undervoltage. Second strike set high-order bits in the CDU, driving the Z-axis (yaw) middle-gimbal readout past 85 deg and down-moding the platform to coarse-align, causing the observed tumble. Nine SM instrumentation measurements permanently lost. Crew restored fuel-cell power to buses at 000:02:22. Anomaly closed; launch weather rules added for later missions.
anomalies.exchange_quote: Air-to-ground (radio) turns, crew report -> CapCom diagnosis (Apollo Flight Journal, Day 1 pt 1; 2nd strike/platform loss at 000:00:52): (1) Conrad: 'Okay, we just lost the platform, gang. I don't know what happened here; we had everything in the world drop out.' (2) Carr: 'Roger. Plus one.' (3) Conrad: 'I got three fuel cell lights, an AC bus light, a fuel cell disconnect, AC bus overload 1 and 2, Main Bus A and B out.' (4, diagnosis) 000:01:36 Carr: 'Apollo 12, Houston. Try SCE to auxiliary. Over.' [reaffirmed 000:01:43 Carr: 'SCE, SCE to auxiliary.'] Tightly-timestamped context: 000:01:33 Conrad (onboard): 'We've got a short on it of some kind...'; 000:01:36 Carr: 'Try SCE to auxiliary.'
anomalies.notes: THE marquee anomaly; the only one turn-hunted. John Aaron (EECOM) recognized the garbled-telemetry pattern and called 'SCE to Auxiliary'; Bean threw the SCE switch and telemetry was restored. Counted 4 air-to-ground turns (2 strictly intervening) from Conrad's report of the electrical emergency to Carr's diagnosis. get_report anchored to AFJ-documented 000:00:52 second strike / platform loss (Conrad's downlinked report immediately followed, not separately inline-timestamped); get_diagnosis 000:01:36 is inline in the transcript; human_time_s=44 is therefore approximate to a few seconds. Report Section 14.1.3 'Electrical Potential Discharges'.

anomalies.symptom: Approximately 1.5 hours before launch the crew reported several intermittent all-8's displays on the command module main display and keyboard assembly (DSKY). No display malfunction occurred in flight.
anomalies.documented_cause: A short across the normally-closed contacts of any one relay in the display relay matrix applies 250 V ac to all segments (common discharge path). Failure analyses after four previous identical failures showed relay contamination as the likely cause. Fabrication moved to laminar-flow clean rooms, 100% vibration screening added, and a malfunction procedure devised to clear a shorted condition. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Report Section 14.1.1. Preflight crew report; cause from prior failure-analysis history, not an in-flight diagnosis.

anomalies.symptom: During cryogenic loading about 51 hours before launch, the heat leak of hydrogen tank 2 was unacceptable; a thick frost layer on the tank exterior verified inadequate vacuum in the insulating annulus. Tank removed and replaced before launch.
anomalies.documented_cause: Incomplete bond in the stainless-steel/titanium bimetallic joint let hydrogen leak from the inner tank into the vacuum annulus. Improper manufacturing inspection (lot 3B; lot 3A suspect) allowed voids to pass. Remaining suspect tanks recalled for joint replacement. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Report Section 14.1.2. Ground/prelaunch cryo-loading anomaly, detected by ground data and visual frost check.

anomalies.symptom: During systems checks after earth-orbit insertion, stabilization-and-control circuit breaker 23 (logic buses 3 and 4, panel 8) was found open. A crewman closed it and it stayed closed for the rest of the mission.
anomalies.documented_cause: Postflight electrical and mechanical tests of the breaker and circuitry were normal; no cause found for launch-vibration or electrical-fault opening. Because it was fed in parallel with two breakers that did not open and showed no abnormalities, the breaker was probably not properly set during prelaunch positioning checks (these breakers are not specifically verified). Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Report Section 14.1.4. Crew found and reclosed it; root cause not determined in flight (postflight conclusion).

anomalies.symptom: The crew reported that two RCS isolation valves (quad A secondary propellant isolation valve and quad B No. 1 helium isolation valve) had inadvertently closed during CSM/S-IVB separation. Crew reopened them per preplanned procedure with no further problems.
anomalies.documented_cause: Same shock-induced closure phenomenon seen on Apollo 9 and 11 for propellant isolation valves; the helium isolation valve closure was the first noted in-flight occurrence. Failure-investigation test programs (postflight). Crew recovery was procedural.
anomalies.notes: Report Section 14.1.5. Crew-reported; recovery procedural, root-cause investigation postflight.

anomalies.symptom: Operation of the S-band high-gain antenna in narrow-beam mode produced ~10-12 dB decreases in both uplink and downlink signal strength on several occasions; first observed in lunar-orbit revolution 1.
anomalies.documented_cause: Documented in Section 14.1.6 as unexpected narrow-beam signal-strength variations (analysis of antenna performance; details in Section 14.1.6).
anomalies.notes: Report Section 14.1.6. Ground/telemetry-observed signal-strength anomaly; detailed root cause not fully extracted.

anomalies.symptom: At end of mission a discrepancy of ~27 pounds of oxygen existed between measured total cryogenic oxygen usage and the calculated combined environmental-control-system + fuel-cell oxygen usage.
anomalies.documented_cause: Cryogenic O2 quantity-accounting discrepancy (Section 14.1.7); fuel-cell O2 usage calculated from produced current and cross-checked against hydrogen consumption. Detailed conclusion not fully extracted.
anomalies.notes: Report Section 14.1.7. Postflight accounting/telemetry discrepancy, not crew-detected in flight.

anomalies.symptom: The hatch, left-hand, and both rendezvous windows of the command module showed considerable contamination as vertical streaks on the exterior surfaces. Crew reported seeing water on the windows during heavy pre-launch rain and water flowing over the windows at tower jettison.
anomalies.documented_cause: Gaps in the boost protective cover (hard-to-soft transition over the left rendezvous window) were not sealed with the required sealant on final installation; rain/water intrusion deposited contamination that streaked the windows. Identified via prelaunch notes and postflight inspection.
anomalies.notes: Report Section 14.1.11. Crew observed water in flight; root cause (unsealed BPC gaps) confirmed on the ground.

anomalies.symptom: During ascent and rendezvous there was a VHF communications problem between the command module and lunar module; only one problem was apparent at the time but there were actually two separate problems. From ~142-1/4 hours, LM-to-CM comm had to be relayed via S-band network.
anomalies.documented_cause: Two separate VHF problems in the CM VHF configuration (LM-aft/CM-right antennas), analyzed postflight (Section 14.1.19).
anomalies.notes: Report Section 14.1.19. Crew experienced degraded VHF in flight; two-fault breakdown established postflight.

anomalies.symptom: After initial in-flight LM checkout, CSM-to-LM electrical current was ~1 ampere higher than expected. Turning off the docking-hatch floodlight circuit breaker returned current to normal.
anomalies.documented_cause: The docking-hatch floodlight is controlled by a plunger switch actuated by closing the hatch (like a refrigerator door). The hatch did not depress the plunger sufficiently to open the switch, so the floodlight stayed powered. Crew verified switch/floodlight operation by manually depressing the plunger.
anomalies.notes: Report Section 14.2.1 (LM). Detected via higher-than-expected bus current (telemetry/electrical), then isolated by the crew.

anomalies.symptom: During preparations for the first EVA, water came from both suit inlet hoses when disconnected. After EVA-1 the Commander reported water in his boots and cold moist air from the suit inlet hose; the LM Pilot noted water drops in his inlet hose.
anomalies.documented_cause: Free water in the suit loop; swapping the water separators gave no improvement. Water dried in the suit before the sleep period with no further problem. Managed operationally in flight (Section 14.2.2).
anomalies.notes: Report Section 14.2.2 (LM ECS). Crew-reported; handled operationally, no in-flight root-cause fix.

anomalies.symptom: Following lunar lift-off the crew reported a master alarm near ascent-engine shutdown; on a later pass behind the Moon the CO2 high-partial-pressure light and master alarm tripped again. Crew selected the secondary LiOH canister, then reselected primary at ground request; erratic CO2 indications continued on either canister.
anomalies.documented_cause: Erratic/faulty carbon-dioxide sensor: ground data showed only a short-duration spike in indicated CO2 partial pressure (i.e., not a real CO2 buildup); indications were erratic regardless of which LiOH canister was in use (Section 14.2.3).
anomalies.notes: Report Section 14.2.3 (LM). Crew-reported and treated in flight as an erratic sensor (ground had them reselect the primary canister), so it qualifies as crew-initiated + diagnosed-in-flight, but the specific air-to-ground exchange was NOT turn-hunted (fetch budget was spent on 14.1.3). Left at -1 per bounded-search rule.

anomalies.symptom: At the start of the second darkness pass after lunar lift-off, the crew reported the rendezvous tracking light had failed.
anomalies.documented_cause: Subsequent switch cycling showed normal power consumption, indicating a corona failure in the high-voltage section of the light. Same failure signature as Apollo 9 and ground testing (previously attributed to high-voltage corona); design modifications had been made after Apollo 9 (Section 14.2.4).
anomalies.notes: Report Section 14.2.4 (LM). Crew-reported; corona-failure conclusion drew on Apollo 9 comparison/analysis (treated as postflight diagnosis).

anomalies.symptom: During initial egress the Commander could not release the modularized equipment stowage assembly (MESA) D-ring deploy handle from its support bracket; it could be rotated but not pulled free. The compartment was deployed by pulling directly on the bellcrank cable.
anomalies.documented_cause: A retention pin at the bottom of the D-ring plugs into a socket with a ball-detent mechanism; apparently either the ball detent bound or the crewman did not fully release it (Section 14.2.5).
anomalies.notes: Report Section 14.2.5 (LM/EVA). Crew-experienced mechanical difficulty; cause analyzed on the ground.

anomalies.symptom: During egress the Commander's portable life support system (PLSS) contacted and tore the forward-hatch micrometeoroid/thermal shield, a potential hazard to the suit.
anomalies.documented_cause: Physical contact between the bulky PLSS and the thin hatch thermal shield during egress. For Apollo 13 and later, shield thickness increased (0.004->0.010 in general area; 0.020->0.040 in standoff) and mounting-hole diameter increased (0.375->0.5 in) to strengthen it (Section 14.2.6).
anomalies.notes: Report Section 14.2.6 (LM/EVA). Damage occurred/observed during egress; fix was a postflight redesign.

anomalies.symptom: The descent-propulsion low-level propellant quantity light illuminated about 20+ seconds earlier than expected during powered descent.
anomalies.documented_cause: The low-level light latches on when any one of four low-level point sensors (one per propellant tank) is uncovered; at activation the gaging system indicated fuel/oxidizer conditions consistent with an early point-sensor uncovering (Section 14.2.7).
anomalies.notes: Report Section 14.2.7 (LM descent propulsion). Crew-observed during descent; detailed cause analyzed on the ground.

anomalies.symptom: The color TV camera gave good coverage for ~40 minutes at the start of EVA-1, then the video showed only white in an irregular pattern in the upper picture and black in the remainder; it never recovered despite repeated crew attempts and was turned off.
anomalies.documented_cause: The secondary-electron-conducting (SEC) vidicon tube was damaged by exposure to extreme light levels (the camera was inadvertently pointed at/near the Sun). Ground tests exposing an Apollo-type image sensor to extreme light reproduced the same failure signature (Section 14.3.1).
anomalies.notes: Report Section 14.3.1 (GFE). Famous 'Al Bean pointed the camera at the Sun' failure; cause confirmed by postflight ground tests.

anomalies.symptom: The crew had difficulty removing the radioisotope fuel capsule from the fuel cask during ALSEP deployment (used to fuel the SNAP-27 RTG).
anomalies.documented_cause: Thermal tests and analyses showed dimensional tolerances can diminish with temperature, causing binding between the latch fitting and the capsule/cask (Section 14.3.3).
anomalies.notes: Report Section 14.3.3 (GFE/ALSEP). Crew-experienced EVA difficulty; cause from postflight thermal analysis.

anomalies.symptom: During ALSEP deployment the lunar surface at the passive seismic experiment site was soft and irregular; a crewman had to tamp a depression with his boots to prepare for deployment.
anomalies.documented_cause: Soft, irregular lunar surface material at the deployment site (Section 14.3.4); an environmental/site condition rather than a hardware fault.
anomalies.notes: Report Section 14.3.4 (GFE/ALSEP). Crew-observed EVA deployment difficulty; cause self-evident (surface conditions).

anomalies.symptom: Sharp bang at ~55:54:53 GET with main-bus-B undervoltage, computer restart and master alarm; cryo O2 tank 2 pressure went to zero, fuel cells 1 and 3 lost power ~2.5 min later, and SM RCS quads showed barberpole (He/secondary-valve) indications.
anomalies.documented_cause: Electrical shorts in the cryogenic O2 tank 2 fan circuit (energized at 55:53:20) ignited the fan-wire insulation; the resulting pressure/temperature rise ruptured the tank line and over-pressurized the vacuum jacket, separating the SM bay-4 outer panel and knocking out two fuel cells. Root cause established by postflight/Review Board investigation.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.1. Crew reported the event ('Houston, we've had a problem') but the physical root cause was determined postflight, not diagnosed in flight; separate MSC O2 Tank 2 Anomaly Report published. Not turn-hunted.

anomalies.symptom: Postlanding ventilation inlet valve found closed (exhaust valve open) by recovery personnel after splashdown; vent handle only partially pulled.
anomalies.documented_cause: Inherent lag between the two flexible control cables meant the vent handle was pulled only partway (~5/16-3/8 in), leaving the inlet-valve locking pin not fully retracted so the inlet valve stayed closed. No mechanical failure or out-of-tolerance parts; caution note added to Apollo Operations Handbook.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.2. Found postflight by recovery forces; closed.

anomalies.symptom: From ~40 h, computer readout of the optics shaft angle fluctuated up to ~0.3 deg in the zero-optics mode; crew confirmed via manual readout that the shaft was actually moving.
anomalies.documented_cause: Most likely high slip-ring/brush resistance in the shaft-axis half-speed resolver (vented to vacuum), injecting a small offset into the zero reference. Judged generic and time/vacuum dependent (recurred nearly identically from Apollo 12); no effect on zeroing accuracy, so no corrective action.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.3. Cause reasoned out postflight; recurrence of an Apollo 12 issue. Closed.

anomalies.symptom: Before the ~55 h TV pass, difficulty acquiring and tracking with the high-gain antenna; ~6 dB uplink / ~17 dB downlink loss and cyclic ~5 s downlink transients (55:00:10-55:00:40).
anomalies.documented_cause: Open at time of report. Most probable cause a short in the stator excitation winding of the antenna C-axis induction potentiometer, shifting the scan-limit function line so the auto-reacquisition logic cycled between the target and the manual setting; failure in the electronics box was ruled out. Analysis in progress, separate anomaly report to follow.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.4; listed OPEN in the report. Cause not diagnosed in flight. A dedicated 'HGA Acquisition Problem - Anomaly Report 2' was published Dec 1970.

anomalies.symptom: During entry the entry monitor system 0.05g light did not illuminate within 3 s of the 0.05g condition; the CMP started the system manually via the backup position.
anomalies.documented_cause: Flight problem could not be duplicated in extensive postflight/thermal testing; most likely the CMP switched to backup too quickly before the light came on, or an intermittent hardware failure that cleared itself during entry. No hardware/procedure change warranted.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.5. Crew acted in real time, but no in-flight diagnosis of cause; inconclusive postflight. Closed.

anomalies.symptom: Postflight inspection found propellant gas had leaked from the gusset-4 breech assembly of the apex-cover jettison system, burning a hole through the aluminum gusset cover plate.
anomalies.documented_cause: Hot (>2000 F, ~14000 psi) propellant gas leaked at the breech-plenum interface, burning through the O-ring and Teflon backup ring. Probable cause a gap in the field-trimmed backup ring (scarf joint has no dimensional control). Fix: material/assembly controls plus a polyimide thermal barrier on future spacecraft.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.6. Pyrotechnic/earth-landing system; found postflight. Closed.

anomalies.symptom: Postflight decontamination found the command module RCS system-1 fuel isolation valve open when it should have been closed (all other propellant isolation valves closed).
anomalies.documented_cause: The fuel-valve closing-coil lead was miswired to an unused terminal-board pin during initial installation. In preflight tests at 28 V the valve still closed via inductive coupling from the oxidizer-valve coil, masking the fault; in flight the bus voltage was too low to close it. Fix: resistance checks on all future CM/SM RCS isolation valves.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.7. Manufacturing miswiring found postflight. Closed.

anomalies.symptom: Potable-water quantity reading fluctuated briefly twice: 98% down to 79% for ~5 min at ~23 h, and from full down to 83.5% (recovering in ~7 s) at ~37 h.
anomalies.documented_cause: Erratic potable-water quantity transducer (also failed on Apollo 8 and 12), characteristically caused by minute contamination on the resistance wafer that clears itself; no contamination or corrosion found on disassembly of the Apollo 13 unit. Measurement is non-critical, so no change.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.8. Telemetry/instrumentation fluctuation; cause reasoned postflight. Closed.

anomalies.symptom: Suit pressure transducer dropped from 6.7 to 5.7 psia at S-II ignition (00:02:45) and thereafter read sluggish and up to ~1 psi low, drifting to 4.1-4.3 psia against a 5.0 psia cabin until deactivation at ~59 h.
anomalies.documented_cause: Internal contamination from electroless-nickel plating flakes (poor plating adhesion to the aluminum base; differential expansion cracks the plating, moisture corrodes the base, flakes enter the variable-reluctance air gap). Also solder flux, glass beads and clean-room fibers found. Determined postflight (also failed on Apollo 12).
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.9. Instrumentation failure diagnosed postflight. Closed.

anomalies.symptom: Postflight inspection found propellant gas/soot had escaped from the left-hand CM electrical circuit interrupter (lower equipment bay); right-hand unit was clean.
anomalies.documented_cause: Worst-case tolerance buildup let the attenuator block over-crush so the piston O-ring entered the breech chamfer, displacing it and venting gas. Analysis concluded gas escapes only after the deadfacing/electrical-disconnect function is complete and harms no adjacent equipment; no hardware change required.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.10. CM/SM umbilical circuit interrupter; found postflight. Closed.

anomalies.symptom: Supercritical helium (descent stage) exhibited a pressure-rise rate ~3x expected (14.9 psi/hr vs ~8) starting in the countdown-demonstration cold soak; in flight the rate climbed after each descent-engine firing to ~33 psi/hr until the burst disc vented at ~109 h (108:54:20).
anomalies.documented_cause: Degradation of the tank's annular vacuum insulation by a trace contaminant (probably hydrogen, ~1e-6 lb) that vaporized during the pre-cold-soak flow check and raised thermal conductivity, giving the abnormal rise rate. Burst disc vented as designed. Screening test added for future tanks.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.2.1. Descent Propulsion System supercritical-helium tank; first seen preflight (CDDT), monitored via telemetry, cause established postflight. Closed.

anomalies.symptom: At 97:14 GET the crew reported a thumping noise and snowflakes venting from descent-stage quadrant 4; all four descent batteries showed ~2 s current transients (97:13:53) with corresponding dc-bus voltage drops and a momentary glycol-pump slowdown.
anomalies.documented_cause: Attributed to a descent-battery event (current surge / electrolyte activity venting from quadrant 4); cross-linked to the battery 2 malfunction (14.2.3). Detailed cause analyzed after the mission rather than diagnosed in real time.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.2.2. Crew-reported in real time, but the report presents the cause as postflight analysis, not an in-flight CapCom diagnosis; not turn-hunted. Closed.

anomalies.symptom: LM descent battery 2 malfunction/fault light with master alarm, first at ~100 h and recurring (e.g., flickering light at ~109 h); the crew reported the master alarm and identified battery 2, while voltages and currents remained normal.
anomalies.documented_cause: False (erroneous) over-temperature-type indication: a short between the temperature-switch wires to ground (or auxiliary-relay contamination) tripped the malfunction light while the battery was healthy - the ground verified normal voltages/currents in flight and told the crew to ignore the light. Likely linked to the descent-stage battery current-surge event (14.2.2).
anomalies.exchange_quote: 109:13:30 CMP: 'Okay, Jack. We've got a MASTER ALARM and we've got a battery light flickering.' 109:13:36 CC: 'Okay. Copy a battery light. What battery?' 109:15:01 LMP: '...The only light I'm getting is on BAT 2.' 109:15:35 CC: 'Okay, Fred. We copy your same old friend, battery 2. Could you give us high bit rate for a while, please?' 109:20:54 CC: '...Voltages and currents look normal on battery 2; so ignore the battery light.'
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.2.3 - the one crew-initiated AND in-flight-diagnosed anomaly. Turn count = 11 air-to-ground transmissions from the crew report (109:13:30) to the CapCom false-indication diagnosis (109:20:54): 13:30 CMP, 13:36 CC, 14:16 CC, 14:25 LMP, 14:39 LMP, 14:54 CC, 15:01 LMP, 15:35 CC, 16:13 CC, 16:19 LMP, 16:23 CC, 20:54 CC(diagnosis). human_time_s = 444 (7 min 24 s). Light first illuminated ~099:50 in an earlier episode where ground had them take the battery off-line to investigate; the definitive 'ignore the light' diagnosis was delivered during the 109 h recurrence quoted here. Source: AS13_TEC.txt.

anomalies.symptom: LM ascent-stage oxygen tank 2 pressure rose during flight, indicating reverse leakage through the shutoff valve from the manifold into the tank (up to ~0.22 lb/hr at 193 psi differential).
anomalies.documented_cause: Rolled/damaged forward O-ring during valve installation (the valve design allows more O-ring compression than the supplier recommends, aggravating rolling as the O-ring passes the manifold port) and/or seat contamination. Preflight leak tests checked only reverse leakage at high pressure and were inadequate.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.2.4. Telemetry-detected pressure rise; cause found postflight. Closed.

anomalies.symptom: LM left-hand window shade showed three large separations/cracks when first placed in the stowed position during flight; ~1/8 in cracks from ~80% of the peripheral stitch holes.
anomalies.documented_cause: Aclar embrittlement: the shade material had low elongation (6-12% vs >25% for the improved material) and cracked from the sewing stitch holes. Future shades use heat-treated/quenched more-ductile Aclar reinforced with Mylar tape.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.2.5. Crew observed the cracks, but cause is a known material issue confirmed postflight, not an in-flight air-to-ground diagnosis. Closed.

anomalies.symptom: The 10-mm lens bumper on the LM 16-mm camera was found separated from the lens during inflight LM inspection; the crew reattached it and it held for the rest of the flight.
anomalies.documented_cause: Loose lens/bumper thread fit (a recurring looseness problem). Fix: swage the bumper mating surface for an interference fit with the 10-mm lens internal threads on future missions.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.3.1. GFE camera equipment; crew self-resolved, cause/fix documented postflight. Closed.

anomalies.symptom: Before 55 h the onboard interval-timer time-period set knob came off in a crewman's hand.
anomalies.documented_cause: The knob set screw loosened; the special gripping compound provided insufficient retention force. Fix: secure the knob to the shaft with a roll pin on future timers.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.3.2. GFE crew equipment; cause found on postflight examination. Closed.

anomalies.symptom: When the crew tried to use the two command-module medical-kit nasal spray bottles, one gave no medication and the other only two or three sprays.
anomalies.documented_cause: A cotton insert (added to slow the spray) combined with needing to squeeze at the cotton location impaired delivery in weightlessness; the returned bottle worked normally in 1 g (still held 2.5 cc after 5-6 sprays). Fix: package nose drops like the eye drops on future flights.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.3.3. GFE medical kit; cause determined postflight. Closed.

anomalies.symptom: Six docking attempts required before the probe capture latches engaged during transposition and docking; probe-to-drogue contact was normal on all attempts and capture should have occurred on the five failed ones.
anomalies.documented_cause: Contamination or debris in the capture-latch mechanism restricting plunger motion, which later became dislodged; probe functioned normally afterward (root cause confirmed postflight).
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.1 (CSM). Crew experienced/executed the repeated docking attempts (crew-initiated), but the contamination cause was determined postflight; in flight they simply achieved a hard dock. Left at -1 (not diagnosed via air-to-ground loop in flight).

anomalies.symptom: CSM high-gain (S-band) antenna showed intermittent tracking / boresight shifts during translunar coast and lunar orbit.
anomalies.documented_cause: Faulty connector to one of the coaxial cables feeding the wide-beam antenna elements (per mission report).
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.2 (CSM). Telemetry/ground-signature detected; not a crew-report diagnostic exchange.

anomalies.symptom: Urine dump nozzle blocked after docking and several times during the mission.
anomalies.documented_cause: Freezing of the nozzle under colder-than-previous thermal conditions; resolved in flight by orienting the spacecraft to expose the nozzle to sunlight, plus procedural water-rinse / extended oxygen purge.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.3 (CSM). Crew-reported and worked in flight, but I did not spend fetch budget locating a discrete report->diagnosis air-to-ground exchange; left at -1 per bounded rule.

anomalies.symptom: Degraded VHF voice quality and erroneous VHF ranging measurements (roughly 5-15 mile errors) during rendezvous.
anomalies.documented_cause: Low signal strength from antenna polarization differences and possible connector issue; ranging improved after terminal phase initiation.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.4 (CSM). Detected via AGC/signal-strength telemetry, not a crew-report exchange.

anomalies.symptom: Entry Monitor System (EMS) 0.05g indicator light failed to illuminate within 3 seconds of activation during entry.
anomalies.documented_cause: Neutral-density filter covering the 0.05g light plus solar reflections obscured the crew's view; crew switched to backup timing.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.5 (CSM). Crew-noticed during entry; the resolution was an onboard crew action within seconds, not a multi-turn air-to-ground diagnostic loop. Left at -1.

anomalies.symptom: Main Bus A could not be disconnected: it remained energized when the motor-driven switches were commanded off at ~800 ft during descent staging.
anomalies.documented_cause: Motor switch stalled with internal contacts remaining closed / motor windings open; confirmed by postflight testing.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.6 (CSM). Cause confirmed postflight (status open in report).

anomalies.symptom: Intermittent main-bus-B circuit breaker for battery C; open circuit between battery C and main bus B.
anomalies.documented_cause: Contact cratering with a white substance holding the breaker contacts apart (postflight continuity checks).
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.7 (CSM). Found in postflight testing, not in flight.

anomalies.symptom: Food preparation (hot water) unit leaked: a water bubble collected on the unit stem after dispensing hot water.
anomalies.documented_cause: Particle contamination in the hot-water valve damaging O-rings at elevated temperature (~150 F); root cause postflight (status open).
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.8 (CSM). Crew observed the leak; cause determined postflight.

anomalies.symptom: Rapid repressurization system required three repressurizations instead of the normal single recharge.
anomalies.documented_cause: Increased leakage rate (~40 cc/min vs 14 cc/min preflight); assessed as normal degradation from surge-tank pressure telemetry.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.9 (CSM). Telemetry-based.

anomalies.symptom: LM ascent battery 5 open-circuit voltage dropped from 37.0 V to 36.7 V at ~62 hours instead of holding constant.
anomalies.documented_cause: Suspected battery cell short / short-to-case or conductive foreign material piercing the cellophane separator (from voltage telemetry).
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.2.1 (LM). Battery-voltage telemetry, not a crew-report exchange.

anomalies.symptom: Spurious ABORT command bit intermittently set in the LM primary guidance computer (appeared on the onboard DSKY and in ground telemetry) during lunar orbit before powered descent; recurred and cleared when the crew tapped the panel near the abort switch.
anomalies.documented_cause: Metallic contamination (loose solder/metal) within the hermetically sealed abort-switch module intermittently shorting the abort command; MIT (Don Eyles) wrote a software patch, uplinked, to make the computer ignore the abort input during descent.
anomalies.exchange_quote: 105:11:05 Haise: "Antares, Houston. What we're looking at there is the abort bit, and it looks set." ... 107:11:06 Haise: "Okay, Ed. And before I start in here, would you try tapping the panel again? The abort bit came back...I guess you've surmised already that we have some sort of a contamination in the Abort switch."
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.2.2 (LM) - the marquee crew/ground-diagnosed anomaly. Report first stated air-to-ground at GET 105:11:05 (Haise/CapCom), contamination diagnosis stated at GET 107:11:06 => elapsed 7201 s. Detection was concurrent: onboard DSKY (crew) AND ground telemetry, so crew_initiated is true-but-shared. human_turns_to_diagnosis left at -1: the span crosses at least one loss-of-signal across lunar-orbit revolutions, so an exact count of intervening air-to-ground transmissions is not rigorously verifiable within budget (an AFJ-section estimate of ~40+ transmissions exists but is unverified; not asserted per the no-invented-turns rule). Source: apollojournals.org/afj/ap14fj/19_day5_troubleshooting_lm_computer.html.

anomalies.symptom: LM S-band steerable antenna lost track nine times (unscheduled tracking interruptions) with 2-3 Hz mechanical oscillation exceeding +/-5 degrees.
anomalies.documented_cause: Unknown intermittent condition (not vehicle blockage, multipath, noise, or amplitude modulation); status open. Crew reset the circuit breaker multiple times.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.2.3 (LM). Cause never determined (open).

anomalies.symptom: LM landing radar behaved abnormally during descent: premature switch to low-range scale at ~6 min, initial slant range ~13,000 ft high, range jump from 32,000 to 25,000 ft.
anomalies.documented_cause: Operation beyond design limits and side-lobe lock-on rather than main lobe; crew recycled the circuit breaker to return to high scale. Cause characterized postflight.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.2.4 (LM). Crew acted during the fast descent event; formal cause (side-lobe lock-on) is postflight.

anomalies.symptom: Loss of the Abort Guidance System (AGS): AGS telemetry lost and DEDA inaccessible, with no warning light or alarm.
anomalies.documented_cause: Power-supply/sequencer-module failure in the abort electronics assembly (possible solder joint / component failure); determined postflight to be a standby-mode failure.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.2.5 (LM). Telemetry dropout; diagnosed postflight.

anomalies.symptom: Crew reported a crack across the address-register glass of the AGS Data Entry and Display Assembly (DEDA).
anomalies.documented_cause: Excessive internal stress, improper mounting, or accidental impact; specific cause unknown.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.2.6 (LM). Crew-reported visual observation only; no diagnostic loop (cause unknown).

anomalies.symptom: Lunar topographic (Hycon) camera ran its shutter continuously in operate and standby modes from ~90 hours onward, causing multiple/over-exposures.
anomalies.documented_cause: Contaminated transistor in the shutter-control circuit with a loose aluminum piece (~0.130 x 0.008 in); imagery degradation seen after 192 frames, confirmed by postflight examination.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.3.1 (GFE). Hycon lunar topographic camera; detected via imagery/telemetry and postflight teardown.

anomalies.symptom: Right EVA glove pulled the hand left and down during the second EVA (not observed on the first EVA).
anomalies.documented_cause: Pressurized-glove design allows various neutral positions; no broken cables. Confirmed by postflight chamber tests.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.3.2 (GFE/EVA). Crew felt it during EVA; cause via postflight chamber tests.

anomalies.symptom: Hasselblad intervalometer double-cycled: heard once by crew and shown in photography as 13 double cycles out of 283 exposures.
anomalies.documented_cause: Random response of the intervalometer to camera-motor current (new camera motor with higher current characteristics); characterized via photographic analysis.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.3.3 (GFE). Crew audio report plus postflight photo analysis.

anomalies.symptom: Commander's voice communications degraded at ~29 hours; restored after replacing the comm adapter.
anomalies.documented_cause: Poor contact between connectors due to small contaminants or improper mating; resolved in flight by substituting the adapter.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.3.4 (GFE). Crew-reported and resolved in flight; did not spend fetch budget locating the discrete report->diagnosis exchange, left at -1 per bounded rule.

anomalies.symptom: Active Seismic Experiment thumper misfired: 13 of 21 initiator attempts fired, 5 misfired, 3 skipped, with excessive switch stiffness on the first several firings.
anomalies.documented_cause: Selector-switch dial repositioning out of detent and dirt on the firing-switch actuator bearing surface; crew overcame by using both hands initially.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.4.1 (ALSEP). Crew-reported/worked on the lunar surface (surface EVA comm loop); not turn-hunted per bounded rule.

anomalies.symptom: Suprathermal Ion Detector Experiment (SIDE) produced erratic/noisy data on turn-on, also disturbing the passive seismic and charged-particle experiments.
anomalies.documented_cause: Arcing or corona within the SIDE equipment prior to dust-cover removal; resolved by commanding x10 accumulation mode and removing the dust cover.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.4.2 (ALSEP). Telemetry-detected, ground-commanded fix.

anomalies.symptom: Lunar Portable Magnetometer (LPM) ribbon cable was difficult to rewind and snarled in 1/6 g; reel rotated freely / no lock during rewind.
anomalies.documented_cause: Cable snarls easily, no provision to lock the reel during rewind, and difficult gloved-hand grip (design/operational).
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.4.3 (ALSEP/EVA). Crew-experienced on the surface; operational finding.

anomalies.symptom: ALSEP central station 12-hour timer failed: timer pulses absent after initial activation; mechanical section operated only intermittently.
anomalies.documented_cause: Mechanical timer design failure (logic functional, mechanical section non-responsive); similar to the Apollo 12 timer issue.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.4.4 (ALSEP). Telemetry / uplink-command verification.

anomalies.symptom: Passive Seismic Experiment horizontal Y-axis leveling motor operated intermittently; 6 of 22 leveling commands unresponsive.
anomalies.documented_cause: Intermittent component in the motor-control circuit (no temperature correlation); ground achieved leveling by a command-cycling technique.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.4.5 (ALSEP). Telemetry-detected.

anomalies.symptom: Passive Seismic Experiment long-period vertical seismometer unstable in filter-in mode, oscillating to saturation.
anomalies.documented_cause: Electrical (not mechanical) failure in the feedback-filter circuitry; resolved by commanding removal of all feedback filters.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.4.6 (ALSEP). Telemetry-detected, ground-commanded fix.

anomalies.symptom: Active Seismic Experiment geophone 3 electronic channel erratic: data spiking off-scale high, channel running at ~30x the gain of the other channels.
anomalies.documented_cause: Intermittent open circuit in the diode feedback path of the logarithmic compressor; suspected solder crack in cordwood construction (status open).
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.4.7 (ALSEP). Telemetry-detected; cause suspected, status open.

anomalies.symptom: Intermittent loss of valid data from the SIDE positive log analog-to-digital converter (full-scale output followed by erroneous values in specific words).
anomalies.documented_cause: Intermittent failure of the start-reset pulse for the positive-log A/D converter control logic.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.4.8 (ALSEP). Telemetry-detected.

anomalies.symptom: Charged Particle Lunar Environment Experiment (CPLEE) analyzer B data lost: analyzer-B power-supply voltage measurement erratic, science data lost (~April 8, 1971).
anomalies.documented_cause: Short circuit in output filter capacitors, interconnecting cable, or analyzer (high-voltage oscillator still functioning); probable short located in postflight/on-orbit analysis.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.4.9 (ALSEP). Occurred on the deployed surface package after the crew departed (April 8, 1971); telemetry-based.

https://www.apollojournals.org/afj/ap15fj/03tde.html (Apollo 15 Flight Journal, Transposition/Docking - SPS Thrust light air-to-ground exchange)

anomalies.symptom: Quad B and quad D SM RCS secondary/primary propellant isolation valve talkbacks intermittently indicated closed (at post-insertion checks, S-IVB sep ~3:22, and SIM-bay door jettison); crew reopened each time.
anomalies.documented_cause: Magnetic-latching isolation valves closed by pyrotechnic shock (a mechanism seen on previous missions); reopened by crew each occurrence.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.1. This atlas lists the 20 most significant of the 44 numbered anomalies in Section 14 of the Apollo 15 Mission Report (18 CSM, 8 LM, 4 SIM, 3 ALSEP/surface, 7 GFE, 4 LRV).

anomalies.symptom: SPS Thrust light on the Entry Monitor System panel illuminated shortly after transposition and docking with no engine firing command present (would have caused ignition if engine armed).
anomalies.documented_cause: Short to ground in the system A delta-V thrust switch within the SPS ignition circuitry; confirmed by test firing at 28:40:22. Ground had crew safe the engine by opening both SPS Pilot Valve circuit breakers.
anomalies.exchange_quote: 003:36:12 Scott (CDR): '...the only different thing we've noticed is the SPS Thrust light on the EMS is now on.' | 003:36:25 Fullerton (CapCom): 'Roger. I understand the SPS Thrust light is on.' | 003:36:28 Scott (CDR): 'And all the switches are off.' | 003:38:44 Fullerton (CapCom): '15, Houston. We'd like you to pull [open] both SPS Pilot Valve circuit breakers on Panel 8.' | 003:38:53 Scott (CDR): 'Okay; that's being done. They're both open.'
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.3. Only clean crew-report -> CapCom-response exchange in the mission. Turn count = 4 air-to-ground transmissions from crew's first report (003:36:12) to CapCom's diagnostic safing instruction (003:38:44); 152 s between those two GETs. Root-cause isolation (delta-V switch short) confirmed later by the 28:40:22 test firing. Source: apollojournals.org/afj/ap15fj/03tde.html.

anomalies.symptom: A-c bus 2 and d-c bus B undervoltage alarms occurred, then the integral lighting circuit breaker opened; DSKY/EMS scroll and other backlighting were lost for the rest of the mission.
anomalies.documented_cause: Short circuit inside the mission timer (shorted input filter capacitor); found in postflight teardown after timer returned to vendor.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.4.

anomalies.symptom: At ~81.5 h the battery relay bus voltage telemetry read 13.66 V instead of nominal ~32 V; crew confirmed low reading on panel 101 test meter, and moving the test-meter switch restored the normal reading.
anomalies.documented_cause: Isolated to instrumentation circuitry; bus functional operation not impaired. No hardware fault duplicated in postflight testing.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.5.

anomalies.symptom: Potable water tank quantity began decreasing during meal prep at ~277 h and failed to refill for the rest of the flight (waste tank kept accepting fuel-cell water normally).
anomalies.documented_cause: Failed check valve in the water management system prevented potable-tank refill (a similar earlier event at 13.5 h had been mis-attributed to a closed inlet valve).
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.7.

anomalies.symptom: Panel 2 mission timer stopped at 124:47:37 and repeatedly failed to restart when the start/stop/reset switch was cycled.
anomalies.documented_cause: Mission-timer internal fault; timer would not restart (separate unit from the panel-1 digital event timer).
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.8.

anomalies.symptom: One of three main parachutes deflated to ~1/5 diameter at ~6000 ft; the CM landed on effectively two chutes. Recovery photos showed 2-3 of 6 riser legs missing on the failed canopy.
anomalies.documented_cause: Postflight/photographic analysis; leading candidate was CM RCS propellant (fuel) burning on the riser lines during the propellant-depletion firing (other candidates: forward heat-shield proximity, a broken riser/suspension-line connector link).
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.9. Most safety-significant Apollo 15 anomaly; separate formal Anomaly Report No. 1 was issued. Detected via recovery/photographic evidence, not crew diagnosis.

anomalies.symptom: The right-side restraint harness on both the center and right crew couches came apart (unscrewed) during lunar orbit; crew reassembled and taped one missing cap in place for landing.
anomalies.documented_cause: Plug-and-cap (bolt with nylon locking insert) on the couch seatpan backed out under repeated back-and-forth rotation.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.12.

anomalies.symptom: With the cabin fans running, the crew heard an object striking the blades; cycling the fans repositioned it. Postflight the blades were gouged.
anomalies.documented_cause: A loose 1/4-inch washer in the fan ducting struck the blades; found in postflight inspection of the ducting.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.13.

anomalies.symptom: LM steerable (S-band) antenna showed random oscillations in auto-track mode, diverging and losing lock on three occasions.
anomalies.documented_cause: Auto-track oscillations driven by vehicle blockage/structural reflections and unfavorable Earth look angles at specific times (100:26, 100:41, 104:07).
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.2.4.

anomalies.symptom: The LM descent engine control assembly circuit breaker was found open during the post-separation engine throttle check; closing it allowed the check to complete.
anomalies.documented_cause: No current surge found in data; report states the most probable cause is that the crew inadvertently left the breaker open (crew statement).
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.2.5. Crew-attributed cause but no locatable CapCom-diagnosis exchange, so turns left at -1.

anomalies.symptom: Abort Guidance System warning and master alarms occurred just after lunar-orbit insertion and again at AOS before LM deorbit; first was reset by crew, second persisted to lunar impact.
anomalies.documented_cause: Momentary out-of-tolerance condition (28 V dc, 12 V dc, or 400 Hz) tripped the warning, which self-resets when back in tolerance; AGS performance was normal throughout.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.2.6.

anomalies.symptom: Before LM ingress the range/range-rate meter window broke; on ingress the crew found many glass particles floating in the cabin (a hazard).
anomalies.documented_cause: Hermetically sealed meter case (He-pressurized) developed up to ~16 psi differential at cabin vacuum; the 0.085-in annealed soda-lime glass window failed from a surface flaw under that stress.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.2.8.

anomalies.symptom: Panoramic camera velocity/altitude sensor telemetry (first pass, rev 4) showed the sensor not operating correctly, drifting off-scale high (saturating) and auto-resetting.
anomalies.documented_cause: Velocity/altitude sensor malfunction; the sensor controls camera cycling rate, forward-motion compensation, and exposure.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.3.1. Telemetry-detected.

anomalies.symptom: Laser altimeter altitude data became intermittent after rev 24 and was fully lost after rev 38.
anomalies.documented_cause: Decreasing laser output power, then the photomultiplier-tube high-voltage supply stuck in idle so the receiver missed surface returns; duplicated on the ground with a buzzing relay pulled from a flight unit.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.3.2. Telemetry-detected.

anomalies.symptom: Multiple problems during ALSEP deep-core/bore-stem drilling: insufficient penetration depth, bore stems hard to release from the drill adapter, bore-stem damage near the first joint, and core stems hard to extract and separate.
anomalies.documented_cause: Bore-stem/joint and flute design plus dense subsurface regolith; extraction and section-separation difficulties addressed by postflight hardware redesign.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.4.1. Well-known Apollo 15 EVA drilling difficulty (Scott/Irwin at the ALSEP site). Worked in real time with the ground but root-cause/fix was postflight.

anomalies.symptom: Lunar-surface 16-mm camera film magazines jammed: 5 of 8 magazines taken to the surface jammed.
anomalies.documented_cause: Drive-spline damage/misalignment: improper installation misaligned the camera's floating female spline with the magazine male spline, removing metal from the brass spline.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.5.3 (government-furnished equipment).

anomalies.symptom: LRV battery 2 volt/ammeter was inoperative from vehicle activation and stayed dead through all traverses.
anomalies.documented_cause: Meter fault not duplicated in any ground test; instrument non-essential to vehicle operation, so anomaly was closed with no further action.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.6.2.

anomalies.symptom: LRV front steering was inoperative at initial activation (powered but wheels would not steer, no motor stall current); it became operative before the second traverse after the crew cycled the forward-steering breaker/switch.
anomalies.documented_cause: Intermittent front-steering fault; cleared itself before traverse 2 and was not isolated in flight (drove first traverse on rear steering only).
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.6.3. Well-known Apollo 15 LRV issue; crew troubleshot with ground but the intermittent cause was never diagnosed in flight, so turns = -1.

anomalies.symptom: LRV seat belts were problematic on all traverses: hooks slipped through handholds to the floor, belts snagged on the GSE connector, and belts were too short to secure easily.
anomalies.documented_cause: Belts sized for a larger pressurized-suit contour; unexpected decrease in suit contour left the belts effectively too short and prone to displacement/snagging.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.6.4.

anomalies.symptom: During the pre-ignition checklist for the lunar-orbit circularization maneuver, an oscillation (limited to +/-1.0 deg at 2.4 Hz) was detected in the yaw axis of the SECONDARY servo loop of the service propulsion engine gimbal actuator; present in all modes but only when the secondary yaw servo loop was used. Delayed powered descent/landing by roughly 6 hours.
anomalies.documented_cause: Failure believed electrical in nature (intermittent open in the secondary yaw servo loop); a case of no oscillation on repositioning implied an electrical fault. Apollo 17 wiring-harness routing changed for strain relief. Mission Control cleared the SPS for use on the PRIMARY system and the landing proceeded.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.10 - the mission's marquee in-flight event (SPS thrust-vector-control / secondary yaw gimbal actuator). CMP Mattingly first reported the oscillation at 097:35:10, but that was a VHF crew-to-crew call to the LM, not an air-to-ground CapCom exchange, and CSM was near LOS behind the Moon. The go-for-landing 'diagnosis' came only after several hours of ground engineering analysis, not a single locatable CapCom exchange, so turns left at -1 per rules.

anomalies.symptom: Abnormally high heat leak into cryogenic hydrogen tank 3, raising heater/fan duty and boiloff.
anomalies.documented_cause: Cause not definitively determined; investigation found the tank had been returned to the vendor for rework and receiving inspection had noted water in the shipping container (possible annulus vacuum/insulation degradation). Anomaly closed without firm root cause.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.5. Telemetry-detected cryogenic EPS anomaly.

anomalies.symptom: Spacecraft failed to respond to uplink real-time commands at 42:23:09 and again at 207:14:36; command capability lost until the crew cycled the up-telemetry command reset switch off and back to normal.
anomalies.documented_cause: Logic lock-up within the up-data link package; only postulated causes are a spacecraft power-system transient or a transient internal to the up-data link. External transients ruled out via telemetry.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.6. Ground detected loss of command capability; crew action (switch cycle) restored it; root cause not fully resolved in flight.

anomalies.symptom: Mass spectrometer boom (SIM bay) stalled and would not fully retract; on the final event it stalled ~two-thirds out (~200 in) and would neither extend nor retract. Boom and experiment jettisoned prior to TEI.
anomalies.documented_cause: Assumed jamming/bunching or snagging of the coiled experiment power cable in the boom housing during retraction; repeated prolonged motor stalls burned out the motor. Data did not reveal a definite cause.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.8. Crew operated the SIM bay and observed the stall; cause assumed, not confirmed.

anomalies.symptom: Gamma ray spectrometer boom mechanism stalled and would not fully retract on three of five retractions (always past the safe SPS-firing position per proximity switch).
anomalies.documented_cause: Most probable cause bunching/snagging of the coiled experiment power cable during retraction (as seen in 1-g ground testing); assumed cable jamming in boom housing. No further action - mechanism not reused.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.9. Companion boom problem to 14.1.8.

anomalies.symptom: High-gain antenna would not acquire; HGA operation lost for a period.
anomalies.documented_cause: Documented in Section 14.1.16 (CSM S-band high-gain antenna acquisition loss).
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.16.

anomalies.symptom: Computer issued an erroneous gimbal lock indication at 38:18:56.
anomalies.documented_cause: Indication was erroneous (spurious); investigated in the inertial subsystem / CDU area.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.3. Related to 14.1.4 inertial-subsystem warnings.

anomalies.symptom: Inertial subsystem warnings and coupling data unit (CDU) fail indications.
anomalies.documented_cause: Documented in Section 14.1.4; associated with erroneous indications in the inertial/CDU electronics.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.4.

anomalies.symptom: Service propulsion system oxidizer tank pressure measurement shifted.
anomalies.documented_cause: Instrumentation/measurement shift (transducer), not an actual propulsion pressure anomaly.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.2. Telemetry/instrumentation.

anomalies.symptom: Lithium hydroxide canister stuck during the first canister change.
anomalies.documented_cause: Documented in Section 14.1.15 (mechanical sticking of LiOH canister).
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.15.

anomalies.symptom: Explosive failure of a ground-support-equipment oxidizer deservicing tank during postflight deservicing operations.
anomalies.documented_cause: Ground support equipment failure during deservicing (not an in-flight spacecraft failure).
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.1.20. Postflight ground event, included in the report.

anomalies.symptom: At lunar lift-off, four vertical thermal shields on the LM ascent-stage aft equipment rack were torn loose from the lower standoffs (remained attached at upper standoffs); observed from lunar-based TV.
anomalies.documented_cause: Most probable cause: ascent engine exhaust entering the cavity behind the shields; the shield projection below the support tube plus insufficient blanket venting allowed pressure buildup exceeding shield capability. Redesign/venting added for Apollo 17.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.2.2 (LM). Observed via ground/TV, analyzed postflight.

anomalies.symptom: LM S-band steerable antenna would not operate (inoperative) in the yaw axis.
anomalies.documented_cause: Traced to the antenna stow-latch/solder-melt release area (marginal electrical conditions letting the housing act as a heat sink); multiple corrective actions planned for Apollo 17.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.2.3 (LM).

anomalies.symptom: During system pressurization at ~95 h, LM RCS system A regulator outlet pressure crept above lockup; helium leaked (rate varying to ~1100 scc/min) throughout the mission, and system A relief valves eventually periodically relieved at ~237 psia.
anomalies.documented_cause: Internal leakage in the regulator assembly; a design deficiency in secondary-regulator lockup under small differential pressure. Crew performed propellant-transfer operations to preserve blowdown capability.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.2.4 (LM RCS helium regulator leakage). Telemetry-detected; managed in flight via propellant transfers but root cause analyzed postflight.

anomalies.symptom: Loss of lunar module attitude control after the (unmanned) jettison.
anomalies.documented_cause: Documented in Section 14.2.6; loss of attitude control occurred after crew egress/jettison.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.2.6 (LM). Post-jettison, unmanned.

anomalies.symptom: Abort guidance system (AGS) out-of-plane velocity error larger than expected.
anomalies.documented_cause: Documented in Section 14.2.7 (LM AGS out-of-plane velocity error).
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.2.7 (LM).

anomalies.symptom: Ascent propulsion system chamber pressure showed an increase and decay during the ascent firing.
anomalies.documented_cause: Documented in Section 14.2.8; analyzed from ascent firing reconstruction.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.2.8 (LM APS).

anomalies.symptom: Command module television camera monitor malfunctioned.
anomalies.documented_cause: Documented in Section 14.3.1 (GFE TV camera monitor malfunction).
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.3.1 (GFE).

anomalies.symptom: After lunar-surface exposure, the wrist ring disconnects on the Commander's and LMP's suits were hard to rotate into the locked position and very difficult to rotate out.
anomalies.documented_cause: Lunar soil (dust) contamination in the small clearance/sliding surfaces of the wrist disconnect; the loose gauntlet let dirt reach the disconnect.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.3.4 (GFE/EVA suit).

anomalies.symptom: Heat flow experiment cable broke when the Commander's legs became entangled in it during ALSEP deployment, resulting in loss of the heat flow experiment.
anomalies.documented_cause: Crew (Young) inadvertently snagged and broke the heat flow experiment cable at the connector; break was self-evident on the surface. No corrective action - experiment not reflown.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.4.1. Crew recognized the cable break immediately on the surface; cause self-evident, so no CapCom diagnosis exchange to count (turns remain -1).

anomalies.symptom: Erratic laser altimeter photomultiplier tube voltage during lunar-orbit operations, degrading altimeter data.
anomalies.documented_cause: Documented in Section 14.5.5; PMT high-voltage anomaly progressively degraded/lost laser altimeter data (related to laser output degradation, 14.5.3).
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.5.5 (orbital experiment / SIM bay laser altimeter).

anomalies.symptom: On the initial drive from the LM, the lunar roving vehicle rear steering was inoperative; the crew drove on front steering only, and rear steering later began working on its own.
anomalies.documented_cause: Cause never determined; rear steering spontaneously became operative later in the traverse (possible cold/viscous lubricant or intermittent connection; report notes numerous failure possibilities in the steering electronics).
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 14.6.2. Crew-detected on the surface but it self-cleared with no formal CapCom diagnosis; cause never found. No crew-report->CapCom-diagnosis exchange to count, so -1.

sources_consulted: https://an.rsl.wustl.edu/apollo/data/A17/resources/A17_MissionReport.pdf (Apollo 17 Mission Report, Section 15 ANOMALY SUMMARY, pp.15-1 to 15-41)
https://apollojournals.org/alsj/a17/a17.alsepoff.html (ALSJ, EVA-1 Flag Deployment and ALSEP Off-Load - cask dome removal exchange)

anomalies.symptom: Several spurious master alarms without accompanying caution/warning lights after earth-orbit insertion; alarms could be initiated by tapping on panel 2; main bus A undervoltage light flickered coincident with one alarm; some alarms coincided with moving the cryogenic pressure indicator switch to position 1/2.
anomalies.documented_cause: Intermittent zero-g-dependent short-to-ground on panel 2 wiring in the main bus A undervoltage / cryogenic pressure indicator circuits; postflight inspection of panel 2 wiring and the reset switch found no contamination. Nuisance only, valid warnings not inhibitable; no corrective action. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 15.1.1. Crew localized the source region (panel 2) in flight by tapping; true root cause never conclusively isolated even postflight. No quoted crew-report->CapCom-diagnosis exchange located within fetch budget.

anomalies.symptom: Lower-equipment-bay mission timer was 15 seconds slow at 1 hour 58 minutes after lift-off; crew reset it and it worked properly for the rest of the mission.
anomalies.documented_cause: Most probable cause an intermittent in one of the timer's integrated circuits, possibly from mechanical imperfections in circuit construction; postflight testing normal. Redundant timers exist; no corrective action. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 15.1.2. Crew reset symptom in flight; cause determined postflight.

anomalies.symptom: Retract limit sensing switch on lunar sounder HF antenna boom 1 failed to operate, giving telemetry and CM display data indicating the boom had not fully retracted (motor current showed it actually had retracted).
anomalies.documented_cause: Confined to the retract limit-switch system (abnormal cam-follower friction, defective spring, hole misalignment, or internal switch malfunction); no most-likely cause established. Device not flown again. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 15.1.3. Telemetry/display-detected.

anomalies.symptom: Lunar sounder HF antenna boom 2 extension at ~191:38 required more time than expected; motor stalled after ~half deployment; motion re-established by cycling the power switch until fully deployed; condition repeated on subsequent extensions.
anomalies.documented_cause: Greater-than-expected motor load from increased/varying friction in the guide/antenna forming assembly in the thermal/vacuum environment (a recurring Apollo mechanism peculiarity). Not used again. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 15.1.4. Crew worked around it by power cycling; cause from postflight analysis.

anomalies.symptom: Entry monitor system accelerometer null bias shifted before the transearth midcourse correction (nominal +0.01 ft/sec2, rose to +0.66, then +0.20 ft/sec2 after the maneuver); the 0.05g light illuminated erroneously during the pre-entry EMS self-test.
anomalies.documented_cause: Candidate causes: contaminant particle/bubble in the accelerometer damping fluid, intermittent open in the temperature-compensation circuit, or intermittent short in the 12-position function switch; none confirmed (postflight tests normal). EMS is a backup; entry procedures revised in flight to circumvent premature 0.05g. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 15.1.5. Crew observed the 0.05g light and revised procedures in flight; root cause never established.

anomalies.symptom: Leakage in and around the chlorine injector casing assembly and occasional difficulty rotating the knob that advances the injector piston; 6 of 13 chlorine and 5 of 13 buffer ampules had bladder tears.
anomalies.documented_cause: A changed bladder-bonding process created a high-stress tension-to-shear transition region so bladders tore at the adhesive-bond periphery when pressurized with the end cap free; a bent injector outer needle also tore gland septums. Skylab/ASTP procedures and needle inspection revised. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 15.1.6. Crew noticed leakage/knob difficulty; cause found postflight.

anomalies.symptom: Photography taken from the LM during rendezvous showed the mapping-camera reaction-control-system plume shield door in the open position with the mapping camera retracted (the spring-loaded door should close on retraction).
anomalies.documented_cause: Problem is with the door itself; friction between sliding metal surfaces likely significantly increased by the space environment (common factor with other Apollo 15/16/17 mechanism anomalies), not duplicated in ground testing. Last mission; no further action. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 15.1.7. Photo-detected postflight/during rendezvous imagery.

anomalies.symptom: Cryogenic hydrogen tanks 1 and 2 automatic pressure operating deadband decreased from ~16 psi to ~3 psi after about 12-13 hours and recurred later; hydrogen pressure then maintained by manual fan operation for the rest of the mission.
anomalies.documented_cause: Hard particles/burrs (from toggle-plate coining) floating in the pressure-switch stop mechanism under zero-g, variably restricting stop travel and shifting the switch set points. Manual control adequate for Skylab/ASTP; no further inspection. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 15.1.8. Telemetry-detected.

anomalies.symptom: Erroneous readings occurred on several command/service module one-sample-per-second measurements between 191:40:39 and 191:42:32; data from two ground stations showed the problem was on the downlink signal (PCM).
anomalies.documented_cause: Problem in the pulse-code-modulation timing pulse network that controls the word matrices; postflight shock and vibration bench tests operated normally. Anomaly left OPEN (workaround considered for Skylab/ASTP).
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 15.1.9. One of the few explicitly left OPEN in the report; telemetry/ground-station detected.

anomalies.symptom: During four early lunar-orbit revolutions the water/glycol temperature control valve failed to open properly as radiator outlet temperature decreased; mixed coolant momentarily fell up to 4 F below the 42-48 F control band during mixing startup.
anomalies.documented_cause: Slight sticking of the valve gear train after being driven hard against the full-closed stop during hot lunar-orbit periods; non-tangent gear pitch circles cause sliding rather than rolling (scraped dry lubricant), raising friction. Self-corrected on later orbits; manual clutch disengagement available. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 15.1.10. Telemetry-detected; self-corrected.

anomalies.symptom: At approximately 108:06 the lunar module battery 3 and battery 4 voltage telemetry differed by ~0.5 V (battery 3 higher); the paralleled batteries should read equal, and no reverse-current battery-malfunction alarm occurred.
anomalies.documented_cause: Battery 4 voltage readout was not a true reading; a ~1% resistance increase in the signal-conditioner input resistive divider network (or a failure in the zero-adjust network) accounts for the offset; battery 4 was actually delivering positive current. Not flown again. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 15.2.1. Telemetry-detected; a measurement (not battery) fault.

anomalies.symptom: While using oxygen demand regulator A for cabin depressurization before the third EVA, data showed the suit loop leaking at 0.04 lb/hr; the crew switched to regulator B for the remainder of the mission.
anomalies.documented_cause: Contamination of the regulator A ball/poppet seat (a ~2.5-micron particle lodged between poppet and seat), or an inadvertently bumped regulator handle (considered unlikely). Not used on future spacecraft. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 15.2.2. Data-detected; crew mitigated by switching regulators.

anomalies.symptom: At 253:44 during preparation for the transearth-coast EVA, the Command Module Pilot (Evans) could not hear the caution/warning tone in his communications carrier, although transmission and reception were normal; he used the Lunar Module Pilot's communications carrier for the EVA.
anomalies.documented_cause: Two of nine pigtail leads (carrying the caution/warning tone and left-earphone circuits) broke ~1/4 inch below the flex-relief potting, from repeated twisting/knotting because the carrier harness was unrestrained (CMP was not wearing the coverall/harness restraint). Skylab training/procedures revised. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 15.3.1 (government-furnished equipment). CMP found the broken leads himself in flight by partially removing the pigtail sleeve after the EVA; no quoted crew-report->CapCom-diagnosis air-to-ground exchange located within the ~2-fetch budget, so turns left at -1.

anomalies.symptom: After initial turn-on, the lunar surface gravimeter sensor beam capacitor plate could not be centered/stabilized between the fixed capacitor plates; even with all masses commanded on, the beam would not move off the upper plate and could only be brought down by caging it against the lower plate.
anomalies.documented_cause: A mathematical error in the 1-g to 1/6-g mass conversion made the sensor mass weights ~2% too light, beyond the +/-1.5% ground-command adjustment range. Beam later balanced by special caging of the mass assembly, but with considerably reduced sensitivity. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 15.4.1. Data/ground-detected; design/calculation error.

anomalies.symptom: Surface Electrical Properties (SEP) receiver temperature rose to ~80 F during the rest period instead of dropping to ~28 F, and dropped only ~8 F between the second and third EVAs instead of the expected 50-60 F.
anomalies.documented_cause: Lunar dust accumulated on the optical solar reflector (mirror) because the Velcro pad bonds holding the Kapton thermal-bag flaps had failed (weak bond from improper bonding preparation), degrading thermal control. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 15.4.2. Telemetry-detected.

anomalies.symptom: Lunar Ejecta And Meteorite (LEAM) experiment temperature ran higher than predicted during the first and second lunar days across all modes and cover configurations; it had to be commanded off at high sun angles to stay within survival limits.
anomalies.documented_cause: Postulated accretion of lunar dust on the east/west sensor film and grid (driven by charge differential near the terminator when the experiment is on) degrading the thermal-control surfaces; science data indicated normal operation. Mitigated by turning the experiment off at each sunrise/sunset. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 15.4.3. Telemetry-detected.

anomalies.symptom: During EVA-1 ALSEP off-load the Lunar Module Pilot (Schmitt) could not remove the RTG (SNAP-27) fuel cask dome with the dome removal tool; the tool rotated the retaining nut but never latched into the dome recess and stripped/chewed up the dome, which was then pried/wedged off with the geology hammer.
anomalies.documented_cause: The removal-tool locking pins did not engage the dome recess (tool not fully inserted/locked), so rotating the tool turned and stripped the threaded dome interface; the sequence is reproducible with broken pins or incomplete pin locking. Cask not flown on future missions. Closed.
anomalies.exchange_quote: 118:46:35 Schmitt: Gene, I need your hammer. 118:46:46 Schmitt: Well, the dome removal tool never latched into the dome, but it turned it. I think it's pretty badly chewed up. 118:47:44 Cernan: Okay, it's off. It's off. 118:47:51 Parker (CapCom): Roger. Once again we have the right solution.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 15.4.4. Crew self-diagnosed in flight (Schmitt) and resolved with the hammer; CapCom (Parker) confirmed the fix rather than diagnosing it. Symptom report (118:46:35) and the diagnostic statement (118:46:46) are consecutive crew utterances 11 s apart, so human_turns_to_diagnosis counted as 1. Source: Apollo 17 ALSJ a17.alsepoff.html.

anomalies.symptom: A stable zero offset appeared in part of the Lunar Atmospheric Composition Experiment (LACE) data on the mid-mass and low-mass channels (occasionally the high-mass channel), from background noise in the detector system; no loss of data but additional data-reduction processing required.
anomalies.documented_cause: Electronic noise coupling between the unshielded high-voltage wires and the unshielded collectors in the sensor package; the offset is affected by sensor voltage level but not by ion-source or multiplier commands. Data usable, condition stable; no corrective action. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 15.4.5. Data-detected.

anomalies.symptom: Telemetry from the second panoramic-camera pass on revolution 13 showed the velocity/altitude sensor output was erratic; the spacecraft override switch (preset V/A voltages) was used for the remainder of the mission.
anomalies.documented_cause: Probable downward shift in the scaling of the sensor output signal, most likely from a component failure within the sensor circuitry. Last mission for the panoramic camera; no further investigation. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 15.5.1. Telemetry-detected.

anomalies.symptom: A mapping-camera telemetry channel whose pulse confirms film exposure failed to produce the exposure pulse at the lower light levels; a processed metric test strip showed the film had actually been properly exposed.
anomalies.documented_cause: Threshold shift in the light-sensor circuitry (photodiode failure, or a change in the amplifier / one-shot multivibrator or the circuitry between them); similar to Apollo 15/16. Last mission for the camera; no further analysis. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 15.5.2. Telemetry-detected; instrumentation-only (imagery unaffected).

anomalies.symptom: The panoramic camera lost its stereo capability 8 minutes before completing its final lunar-orbit photographic pass; two independent telemetry points showed the lens assembly had ceased to gimbal; monographic photography continued but with degraded forward-motion compensation.
anomalies.documented_cause: Failure in the gimbal drive motor (limited-life motor brushes, most likely) or its power circuitry. Last mission for the camera; no further analysis. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 15.5.3. Telemetry-detected.

anomalies.symptom: Both ultraviolet spectrometer internal temperature measurements (electronics and motor) failed simultaneously near 282:20, with input current increasing ~4%; science data was unaffected and an external case-mounted temperature sensor continued to work.
anomalies.documented_cause: Failure of a component or a wiring short in the +1-volt reference or the -15-volt supply (circuits common to both temperature signal conditioners), consistent with the simultaneous 1-second failure and current rise. Only mission for the instrument; no further analysis. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 15.5.4. Telemetry-detected; housekeeping-only.

anomalies.symptom: After nominal first and third extensions, all other mapping-camera deploy and retract times were longer than expected, behavior similar to the Apollo 15 and 16 missions.
anomalies.documented_cause: Cause not identified despite extensive Apollo 15/16 investigations and precautionary fixes (no-back device removal, improved contamination covers, drive-screw lubricant change); most likely increased friction between sliding metal surfaces from a hard vacuum unobtainable in ground testing (common SIM-bay mechanism factor). Last mission for the device. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 15.5.5. Telemetry-detected; unresolved root cause carried over from Apollo 15/16.

anomalies.symptom: PCM and voice subcarriers lost at ~65:00:00 on the secondary S-band transponder; downlink telemetry/TV time-shared on FM until crew manually switched to alternate transponder
anomalies.documented_cause: Most likely the transponder select switch (directly above the antenna select switch) was inadvertently thrown during frequent antenna switchings without the required OFF-position hesitation, turning both transponders ON; postflight X-ray, bench, vibration and temperature tests of switch and transponder were all negative. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 11.1. Detected by ground-received PM signal-strength drop; crew corrected by switching transponders but root cause is postflight speculation.

anomalies.symptom: Several biomedical instrumentation leads broke or disconnected in flight; one dc-dc converter on the suit harness was reported by the crew to be physically hot (crew removed the harness)
anomalies.documented_cause: Wire breakage from stiff Teflon insulation and stress-concentrating potting; inline connectors allowed disconnects; connector ends corroded with salt deposits. Worst-case dc-dc converter reached only 120F in ground test. Fixes (PVC insulation, softer potting, eliminated inline connectors) are postflight. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 11.2. Crew reported hot converter and removed harness in flight; full diagnosis postflight.

anomalies.symptom: Trigger on the water metering dispenser (water gun) became sticky and hard to operate; postflight activation force 11 lb vs 4 lb spec
anomalies.documented_cause: Forward (metering) O-ring swelled 0.004-0.013 in oversize due to sodium hypochlorite in the drinking water; O-ring material changed to ethylene propylene. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 11.3. Crew-reported symptom; cause found postflight.

anomalies.symptom: Total attitude on FDAI no.1 shifted ~160 deg in pitch when attitude source switched from G&N to SCS; first shift noted by crew ~1 min after switching, immediate on later attempts
anomalies.documented_cause: A tin/silver solder ball found in a switching relay (in the electronic display assembly) that selects sine/cosine resolver outputs; large enough to cause the shift except the 1-minute delay. Could not be reproduced with flight hardware. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 11.4. Crew-noted; diagnosis via ground/postflight relay teardown.

anomalies.symptom: Rotation hand controller no.2 failed to generate the second of a series of minus-pitch minimum-impulse commands; engines fired with no controller movement when mode switched to acceleration command; self-corrected after several hours
anomalies.documented_cause: Probable temporary failure of a breakout microswitch to open (sticky cam operation, a known tendency of this controller design); not reproduced postflight. Later spacecraft (103+) use improved design. Redundant controllers prevent capability loss. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 11.5. Crew-observed; cause postflight.

anomalies.symptom: Entry monitor system delta-V and range-counter circuits malfunctioned prior to lift-off and intermittently in flight (range self-test failed; a 'nine' appeared in the most-significant delta-V digit on switching)
anomalies.documented_cause: Poor/high-resistance solder and internal wire-crimp connections (quality problems); range malfunction later disappeared during thermal cycling, delta-V repeated by pressing an internal crimp. Accepted for flight as non-critical. Anomaly slated to close 18 Dec 1968.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 11.6. Predominantly prelaunch/ground self-test detection; postflight quality diagnosis.

anomalies.symptom: Photographs during revolution 2 showed the +Y SLA adapter panel open only ~25 deg (others ~45 deg); by revolution 19 all four panels were at the normal ~45 deg
anomalies.documented_cause: Panel fully deployed initially then rebounded because its outside retention cable (cork/aluminized-tape wrapped, force-fit in the channel slot) hung up; when the cable later released, slack reeled in and the panel stayed open. Future missions jettison panels (no retention cable). Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 11.7. Detected by photo analysis, not crew report.

anomalies.symptom: Crew reported command module window fogging from a film that built up on the glass during the mission
anomalies.documented_cause: Outgassing of room-temperature-cured RTV used in the window area on the edges of the insulation between heat shield and pressure vessel (same as Gemini); duplicated in ground altitude/elevated-temperature tests. Parts to be vacuum pre-cured on CM 104+. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 11.8. Crew-reported; cause via postflight examination.
