anomalies.symptom: High-level commutator in the command module failed ~5 min after turn-on prior to CM/SM separation; lost time-sequencing and cycled through only 18 of 90 data channels; ~15 min of entry data unrecoverable
anomalies.documented_cause: Not duplicated in extensive postflight testing (voltage, vibration, acceleration, temperature, corona, vacuum, EMI). Suspected EMI; adverse EMI test planned. Not used on future CSMs (used on LM-3). Closeout pending.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 11.9. Telemetry-detected (loss of channel sequencing).

anomalies.symptom: Water leak observed at the B-nut connection to the waste-water overboard quick disconnect during overboard dumps
anomalies.documented_cause: Poor metal-on-metal seal at the B-nut connection to the waste-water overboard quick disconnect; Apollo 8+ uses an O-ring instead. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 11.10. Observed in flight during dumps; cause postflight.

anomalies.symptom: Crew reported two AC bus 1 failure indications and one AC bus 1 and 2 failure indication early in the mission; loss verified on onboard meter, restored by resetting AC bus sensors; occurrences coincided with automatic cryo O2 tank fan/heater cycles
anomalies.documented_cause: Corona arcing of AC power within the motor-operated cryogenic fan switch in the service module: an environmental-seal leak dropped internal pressure to the corona threshold as contacts opened. In flight, a procedural change to prevent both tanks' fans cycling simultaneously stopped recurrence for the remaining ~200 h; root corona cause confirmed postflight (a sister switch leaked 7x spec). Manual fan switching adopted. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 11.11. CREW-DIAGNOSED candidate: crew reported the indications and the in-flight correlation with cryo-fan cycling drove a procedural fix. Turn-hunt attempted (NASA AFJ ap07fj day1 URL redirected to a generic resource page; no clean crew-report -> CapCom-diagnosis exchange with GET timestamps located within the fetch budget). Left at -1 per hard rules (no verbatim timestamped exchange). A PAO transcript exists at honeysucklecreek.net/msfn_missions/Apollo_7_mission/A7_PAO_transcript.pdf for future hunting.

anomalies.symptom: In-flight charges on entry batteries A and B returned 50-75% less energy than expected; planned charge levels could not be maintained
anomalies.documented_cause: High spacecraft charging-circuit (charger-to-battery line) resistance reduced the charging potential; not previously evaluated. Determined analytically on Apollo 7; preflight/inflight/postflight tests with actual circuit resistances reproduced the low energy return. Future spacecraft check individual charger characteristics with line drop. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 11.12. Telemetry/data-detected battery charge shortfall; analytical diagnosis.

anomalies.symptom: At CM/SM separation the crew reported caution/warning undervoltage indications, with main buses A and B at 25.0 and 25.1 V (up to 4.5 V lower than expected); recovered above alarm level (~26.2 V) in ~5 min
anomalies.documented_cause: Low-voltage condition from the batteries' mid-range state of charge, low temperature, and zero-g displacement of electrolyte from the plates. Apollo 8 mitigations: warm batteries on main buses ~12 min before separation, gimbal motors on, remove fuel cell 2; and change battery separator to absorptive cellophane. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 11.13. Crew-reported C&W indication at separation; cause analytical/postflight.

anomalies.symptom: Before the 5th SPS maneuver, fuel cell 2 condenser exit temperature rose to 180F (nominal 155-165F); load removed ~54 min to cool; thereafter every load increase drove fuel cell 2 exit temp to 180-190F
anomalies.documented_cause: Malfunctions in the respective secondary bypass (shuttle) valves, per flight data; postflight, similar erratic shuttle-valve operation reproduced with intentional contaminants. Apollo 8 radiator loop drained/flushed/reserviced; filter/valve-protection studies underway. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 11.14. Telemetry-detected temperature rise, managed in real time (load shedding); bypass-valve diagnosis from flight-data analysis. Not counted as a crew-diagnosed air-to-ground exchange.

anomalies.symptom: During postflight testing, high leakage observed through the closed CM RCS oxidizer propellant isolation valves; valves opened when voltage was removed instead of staying closed
anomalies.documented_cause: Bellows damaged by hydraulic hammering during system activation (valves were closed at activation, an unqualified condition), causing the spring/bellows-preloaded valve to open when de-energized. Corrected by procedure: open isolation valves before CM RCS activation. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 11.15. Discovered in postflight testing.

anomalies.symptom: About 7 min after lift-off, voice communications became garbled and erratic through several ground-station handovers until Simplex-A was selected at ~19 min
anomalies.documented_cause: Improper ground patching procedures and/or malfunctioning receivers at the network stations (e.g., Grand Bahama and Bermuda both patched to air-to-ground 1; VHF uplink not transmitted). Future missions patch voice at a single point at Goddard. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 11.16. Ground-segment/procedural problem noticed in flight as garbled voice.

anomalies.symptom: Under low, variable heat loads the primary water evaporator operated erratically in automatic mode (apparent wick drying and flash freezing); crew repeatedly serviced it with water, then turned it off
anomalies.documented_cause: Automatic-control thermodynamics cause dryout under low cyclic heat loads (as demonstrated with a similar evaporator and verified postflight with the flight unit). Fix: remove sponge material at the boiler-wick temperature sensors to improve response; implemented on CM 106+. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 11.17. Crew observed and managed in flight; corrective mod postflight.

anomalies.symptom: Moisture condensed on ~200 in of uninsulated coolant lines (radiator-to-ECU and ECU-to-IMU); crew dumped it overboard using the urine transfer hose and cabin enrichment purge assembly
anomalies.documented_cause: Condensation on uninsulated coolant lines; the condition was anticipated. Urine transfer hose acceptable for removing free water; lines insulated on spacecraft 106+. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 11.18. Crew handled in flight and cause was anticipated/known (so diagnosed_in_flight=true), but there is no diagnostic air-to-ground exchange to hunt; left at -1.

anomalies.symptom: A seam on three food bags split and the crew reported some food crumbled badly
anomalies.documented_cause: Defective food bags; for future missions the menu will be changed and food bags inspected for defects. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 11.19. Crew-reported crew-provisions issue.

anomalies.symptom: Entry battery manifold pressure increased to cabin pressure (5 psia), indicating a leak from the cabin into the battery manifold
anomalies.documented_cause: Leak associated with undertorqued B-nut fittings (as seen on spacecraft 2TV-1); postflight leak rate was within spec (B-nuts excluded, batteries removed). Future B-nuts torqued to spec. Crew has manual control of the manifold overboard vent, so no hardware change. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 11.20. Telemetry-detected (manifold pressure rise).

anomalies.symptom: Sometime during the mission both primary lamps failed in the lower-equipment-bay floodlights
anomalies.documented_cause: Lamp cathodes (filaments) vaporized, raising start-up voltage from ~500 V toward ~1800 V and shorting a 700-V-rated diode in each lamp driver; deterioration worst near mid-rheostat setting. Procedural change (use secondary lamp on full-bright in ground tests). Anomaly still open.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 11.21. Crew-observed lighting failure; cause postflight; listed as still open in the report.

anomalies.symptom: Glass on both mission event timers cracked during the mission, though timer operation was unaffected
anomalies.documented_cause: Cause pending failure analyses; interim fix for Apollo 8 is transparent tape over the glass. Mission effectivity of further action pending analysis.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 11.22. Crew-observed; cause not yet determined at report time.

anomalies.symptom: Approximately 290 lb of water was found in the docking tunnel
anomalies.documented_cause: Leakage through a makeshift ball check valve installed in the top hatch (the normal tunnel pressure-control valve had been rendered inoperative); upper-hatch vent-valve leak 0.5-3.0 gal/min in stable I. No other spacecraft has this peculiarity. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 11.23. Found postflight.

anomalies.symptom: Recovery forces reported the VHF recovery beacon signal was not received while the spacecraft descended on the main parachutes; beacon received after return to stable I
anomalies.documented_cause: No conclusive cause; beacon and antenna operated properly in postflight test, but the antenna was bent and may not have deployed properly until after return to stable I. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 11.24. Detected by recovery forces (ground), not crew diagnosis.

anomalies.symptom: Crew reported a gurgling sound in the suit supply hoses and observed water droplets at the hose endings (no crew discomfort or hazard)
anomalies.documented_cause: Free water from the water separator not operating properly and/or the cyclic accumulator not being cycled properly (often left in manual mode); separator flow rate measured erratic (0.2-15 lb/hr), cause under study. Future procedure: run accumulators in automatic mode. Closure awaits separator flow-rate study.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 11.25. Crew-reported; cause still under study at report time.

anomalies.symptom: Electromagnetic interference events: mission event timer started inadvertently (coincident with an O2 fan cycle), a computer program alarm appeared when interior lights were brightened, and the central timing equipment showed an unexpected reset
anomalies.documented_cause: Electromagnetic interference / voltage transients (timer starts and program alarms previously seen in ground tests); nuisance-level, no performance degradation, no hardware changes warranted. Central timing updated and operated normally afterward. These problems closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 11.26. Mix of ground-test and in-flight EMI nuisance events; not crew-diagnosed.

anomalies.symptom: Four abnormal Entry Monitor System (EMS) indications: (1) delta-V counter jumped 100 ft/sec during spacecraft/S-IVB separation; (2) after the 3rd midcourse correction the system counted to zero at cutoff then kept counting until crew turned it off; (3) rapidly switching mode from standby to automatic made the delta-V counter jump 19-20 ft/sec; (4) during initial entry the g/velocity scroll trace showed two short incorrect g transients.
anomalies.documented_cause: Postflight tilt-table testing reproduced abnormal accelerometer outputs; inspection found a bubble in the accelerometer damping fluid (case held 1 cc less fluid than filled), with fluid leaking past the O-ring seal near the fill port. Bubble explains the erratic g trace, the random pulses, and the slow drive-to-null after the midcourse correction. Separation counter jump attributed to a logic-race in the sign-change circuit when the counter reads near zero. Seal changed from screw to plug type for CSM 106 and subsequent.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 12.1. Crew observed the abnormal EMS indications in flight but the root cause (damping-fluid bubble/leak) was determined only in postflight functional and tilt-table tests. Report states anomaly still OPEN, Anomaly Report to be prepared.

anomalies.symptom: Visibility through the hatch window degraded to uselessness for visual observation and photography after ~6 hours; the two side windows (1 and 5) fogged to a lesser degree; the two rendezvous windows (2 and 4) stayed usable throughout.
anomalies.documented_cause: Outgassing of silicone oils from the RTV window-sealing material condensing on the inner heat-shield pane, consistent with the Apollo 7 window-fogging analysis. Corrected by a new RTV curing process that greatly reduces residual oils; CM 104 windows 1, 3, 5 refitted with the new-process insulation.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 12.2. Crew-observed condition; cause already understood from prior Apollo 7 analysis rather than diagnosed in flight. Anomaly CLOSED.

anomalies.symptom: On the sixth mission day the cabin fans were momentarily turned on and the crew reported that both fans were noisy.
anomalies.documented_cause: Postflight acoustic measurements at all couch/head, work-station and sleep positions found the fan noise level normal versus prior checkout; no blade or bearing damage, no loose objects, no nicked blades (unlike Apollo 7). Noise possibly a resonant condition in the duct system; no further action required because fans are not needed for a comfortable cabin environment.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 12.3. Crew-reported in flight; assessed as normal in postflight testing. Anomaly CLOSED.

anomalies.symptom: The Commander reported that his left shoulder was showered with water at landing, implying sea water entered through the cabin pressure relief valve; crew reported both sides of the valve had been positioned closed per checklist.
anomalies.documented_cause: Postflight testing: valves held to spec at 13 psi closed, only a fine spray at 25 psig with no permanent yield, no salt deposits, cam/lever rigging verified; only negligible sea water could enter by ram effect. The water that drenched the Commander was most likely accumulated internal condensation (Apollo 7 accumulated ~2 quarts on the aft bulkhead) on uninsulated coolant lines. No corrective action required.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 12.4. Crew-reported at landing; source (condensation vs sea water) determined postflight. Anomaly CLOSED.

anomalies.symptom: Two of the six steel cables in the command module recovery loop failed while the spacecraft was being hoisted from the sea.
anomalies.documented_cause: Known weakness: the recovery loop had shown numerous failures in tests at snatch loadings equivalent to a 32,000-lb load, so an auxiliary nylon loop (installed by swimmers) with adequate margin was already provided. For CM 108 and subsequent the steel cable is replaced by a nylon recovery loop; until then swimmers install the auxiliary nylon loop.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 12.5. Occurred during post-splashdown recovery/hoisting, not detected by the flight crew in flight. Anomaly CLOSED.

anomalies.symptom: During recovery operations the swimmers were unable to communicate with the crew via the intercommunications system; the crew reported the spacecraft intercom switches were in the proper position.
anomalies.documented_cause: Postflight test of the actual swimmer interphone in the recovery configuration gave satisfactory two-way comm to all three crew stations. Most probable cause is outside the spacecraft, associated with operation of the swimmer interphone; interphone-operation training to be emphasized for future flights.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 12.6. Post-splashdown recovery-operations problem, external to the spacecraft; not a flight-crew inflight diagnosis. Anomaly CLOSED.

anomalies.symptom: The potable water tank quantity measurement became erratic at 143:53:00 GET. (No actual water leak occurred - correct water quantity was later drained and leak checks were within spec.)
anomalies.documented_cause: Disassembly found corrosion in the indicator housing, on the variable resistor, and on the actuator pulley, indicating moisture (urine and possibly waste water) had migrated through the oxygen bleed filter/orifice into the indicator housing and bladder when the tank was full (>~90%, bladder isolates the 20-psig oxygen from the bleed orifice, lowering gas-bladder pressure and letting urine/water in during dumps). Moisture in the variable resistor produces erratic readings. For Apollo 9, potable water fill will be terminated at ~80% of maximum.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 12.7. Instrumentation/measurement anomaly noted at a specific GET; root cause (contamination/corrosion) found only on postflight disassembly. Anomaly CLOSED.

anomalies.symptom: Degradation in fuel cell performance experienced after switching to onboard cryogenics during countdown; gas samples from the fuel cell purge lines showed approximately 8000 ppm nitrogen (spec limit 30 ppm).
anomalies.documented_cause: During ground LOX servicing a facility LOX line leak caused a safety shutdown; the vent/shutdown procedure was incorrect in one step, calling for opening valve 1 instead of valve 2, which let liquid nitrogen flow through valve 1 into the LOX supply line and thus into the fuel cell reactant. Procedures were corrected and verified by test.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly 12.8. Pre-launch/countdown ground-servicing event detected by gas sampling; not a flight-crew inflight anomaly. Anomaly CLOSED.

anomalies.symptom: About 2 hours into his first rest period (~11:00:00 GET) the Commander (Borman), after taking a 100-mg Seconal sleeping tablet, awoke nauseated with a moderate occipital headache; nausea worsened with retching and vomiting twice, plus gastrointestinal distress/loose bowels; symptoms remitted within ~24 hours.
anomalies.documented_cause: Tentatively diagnosed in flight by the (chief) medical flight controller as acute viral gastroenteritis (a 24-hr intestinal flu; a 24-hr viral gastroenteritis epidemic was present at Cape Kennedy just before launch); postflight the Commander suggested the symptoms may instead have been a side effect of the sleeping tablet (he had a mild hangover/nausea in preflight trial of the drug). Illness remitted completely with no further treatment.
anomalies.notes: SUPPLEMENTARY - from Section 10 Biomedical Evaluation, NOT one of the 8 numbered Section-12 anomalies (so excluded from anomaly_count_in_report=8). This is the classic crew-diagnosed-in-flight Apollo 8 event, but the tentative diagnosis was made by the medical flight controller from a DELAYED-TRANSMISSION recorded voice dump, not a discrete GET-timestamped CapCom air-to-ground back-and-forth. Per the hard rule (turns require a quoted GET-timestamped transcript exchange), human_turns_to_diagnosis left at -1; not hunted further (bounded). Also note all three crew experienced mild motion sickness early in the mission (Section 10).

anomalies.symptom: Following S-IVB separation the crew lost the ability to translate left during transposition/docking; quad C primary+secondary and quad D secondary propellant isolation valve talkbacks showed barber-pole (closed). Control problem lasted ~12 min.
anomalies.documented_cause: Isolation valves found closed; most probable cause a valve closure from mechanical shock at CSM/adapter separation (spring-loaded, magnetically-latched Parker valves). Investigation inconclusive but hardware undamaged; procedures changed to verify valve indications after shock. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.exchange_quote: 003:04:43 Scott: '...We got turned off, turned around, and lined up, and didn't have any left translation for some reason.' 003:05:00 Roosa: 'Roger. Copy, No left translation.' 003:07:27 Scott: '...for some reason we noticed that we didn't have any left translation and tried to figure out why. Finally noticed that the primary quad C and secondary quad C isolation valves were closed, and the secondary Dog was closed... It took us a while to get back after we got that sorted out...' 003:08:21 Roosa: 'Roger, Apollo 9. Copied all that real good.'
anomalies.notes: CREW SELF-DIAGNOSIS. The crew identified the closed quad C isolation valves onboard during the maneuver (before/at this comm pass) and reopened them without ground help; CapCom Roosa only acknowledged. Turns-to-diagnosis therefore = 0 (no air-to-ground exchange contributed to the diagnosis). The 164 s span is from the crew's first symptom mention (003:04:43) to their self-diagnosis recap (003:07:27); the intervening exchanges concerned an unrelated quad A package-temperature check (~200 F). Further ground discussion occurred at 007:20:18 per AFJ note.

anomalies.symptom: Scanning telescope shaft stuck intermittently during first 5 days; mechanical counter shaft became inoperative on day 2 (degree indicators would not move).
anomalies.documented_cause: Pin on the 'tenths' drum dropped out of an out-of-tolerance (oversize) hole on the drive hub and jammed/lodged in the anti-backlash gears. Crew freed the shaft via repeated manual-adjust operation; root cause established by postflight teardown. Counters replaced on subsequent CM/LM. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Crew operated/freed it in flight but the causal diagnosis (out-of-tolerance hole, dislodged pin) came from postflight teardown.

anomalies.symptom: Automatic pressure control of the cryogenic hydrogen tanks failed; heaters did not auto-activate at ~93 hr, then all H2 heaters came on near final undocking and over-pressurized tanks to ~270 psia, requiring manual heater-off.
anomalies.documented_cause: Most probable cause an intermittent open-circuit in the motor control circuit (16-gage terminal board) induced by undocking shock. Managed manually for rest of mission; no corrective action for Apollo 10. Closed.
anomalies.notes: First indication noted at 93 hr via heater/pressure behavior (telemetry-detected); cause from postflight analysis.

anomalies.symptom: During initial undocking the docking probe did not physically unlatch until the third try; later, with the switch in RETRACT the display showed barber-pole (probe not cocked for docking).
anomalies.documented_cause: Extend/release-retract switch not held long enough for the probe to fully extend/cock; design allows latches not to cock if release motors are not energized long enough. Crew cycled the mechanism to get proper (gray) indication. Operations Handbook changed. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Crew resolved operationally in flight, but the causal diagnosis was ground/postflight analysis; not turn-hunted (Day 4 undocking, ~92-93 hr).

anomalies.symptom: Spacecraft/ground command (uplink) system malfunctioned beginning ~109 hr; over 50% of 55 real-time commands not accepted until crew cycled the up-telemetry command/reset switch at ~118:45.
anomalies.documented_cause: No single cause identified; contributing ground conditions (uplink modulation off, decommutator out-of-lock, marginal RF). Low-voltage 'hang-up' of the updata-link program counter reproduced only under special tests but ruled unlikely in flight. Recycle switch to recover. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Ground-detected (commands not accepted); crew action was corrective, not diagnostic. Cause never specifically identified.

anomalies.symptom: Entry Monitor System failed to scribe during entry.
anomalies.documented_cause: Scribe coat hardened (moisture ingress via a leaking scroll environmental seal, then slow vacuum-dry at 5 psia over 10 days) so the stylus failed to scribe; Loc-tite contamination on the stylus holder added lag. Corrective changes on CM-106+. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Detected/diagnosed postflight via scroll analysis.

anomalies.symptom: Eight master alarms from the propellant utilization & gaging system during the 3rd SPS firing indicating excessive propellant unbalance; crew switched to the auxiliary (point-sensor) system.
anomalies.documented_cause: All alarms explainable: capacitance-tube level not settling as fast as expected at start-up, plus an electrical zero bias in the oxidizer measuring circuit after storage-tank depletion, plus a legitimate unbalance. PUGS master-alarm/C&W functions cut on SC-106+. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Crew reacted (switched to aux) but the alarm causes were explained postflight.

anomalies.symptom: A master alarm with no caution-and-warning annunciator occurred coincident with (hard) docking; additional unexplained master alarms at deorbit (240:31:20) and after drogue deploy (240:55:45).
anomalies.documented_cause: Not determined. Attributed to a shock-sensitive intermittent external input to the very sensitive (5-microsecond) master-alarm trigger among 69 inputs (e.g., intermittent wiring, shock-sensitive transducer, or system transient). No C&W unit malfunction found in postflight tests. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Cause could not be determined; not diagnosable in flight.

anomalies.symptom: Fuel cell 2 condenser exit temperature repeatedly ran outside the normal 155-165 F range (but never above 200 F) between ~88 and ~191 hr.
anomalies.documented_cause: Coolant-loop contamination (gelatinous phosphates/solid particles) restricted secondary coolant regenerator bypass-valve travel. Block I (less contamination-prone) valve to be used on SC-110+. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Telemetry-detected; cause from ground tests/analysis.

anomalies.symptom: Service-module docking (exterior) spotlight failed to operate/deploy; reported by the CMP during the pre-rendezvous lighting check.
anomalies.documented_cause: The deploy circuit breaker was open at launch (per spec, to prevent inadvertent deployment) and had not been closed before the deploy attempt; crew checklist omitted closing it. Checklist changed. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Crew reported; root cause (open breaker / checklist omission) established by ground review.

anomalies.symptom: Crew reported three interior floodlight anomalies: a failed lamp (RH lower equipment bay), a headrest floodlight that overheated with a burning odor, and a failed LH headrest secondary lamp.
anomalies.documented_cause: RH-bay primary lamp: total cathode erosion (mechanical bond failure). Headrest 'overheat/odor': normal hot operation of the lens plus odor from touch-up paint (no actual failure). LH headrest secondary lamp: broken wire in the CM. Procedures/notes added. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Diagnosed by functional postflight testing.

anomalies.symptom: On two occasions the command module computer appeared not to receive/act on data entered via the DSKY (a DAP config change before the 6th SPS burn, and a Verb 46 ENTER to deactivate the autopilot).
anomalies.documented_cause: No hardware failure (computer did blank the displays). Both symptoms reproducible by procedural error: pressing PROCEED instead of ENTER in case 1, and a VERB re-keying or a no-action verb in case 2. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Attributed to procedural error via postflight analysis.

anomalies.symptom: Repressurization of the (ECS) surge tank took an excessive length of time; nominal repressurization achieved after the crew repositioned the tank shutoff valve.
anomalies.documented_cause: Decal marking misaligned with the valve detent position (found ~20 deg off postflight); no mechanical valve problem. SC-106 checked for alignment. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Crew suspected decal misalignment, but this was stated during the postflight systems debriefing; confirmed postflight.

anomalies.symptom: After recovery, one docking-ring separation shaped-charge holder was found deformed and out of its channel, protruding several inches beyond the tunnel structure (a parachute-line hazard).
anomalies.documented_cause: Free end of the pinned charge holder had only weak cantilever spring retention and came out of the backup-ring channel after the ring was cut; qualification tests had shown holders coming out. Whether the distortion occurred in flight or during recovery is unknown (recovery suspected - no heat discoloration). Retention springs added on SC-106. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Found during postflight/recovery inspection.

anomalies.symptom: During the first ~35 s of the first (docked) descent-engine firing, the DPS regulator outlet manifold pressure dropped from 235 to 188 psia (should regulate at 247); supercritical helium tank pressure fell 743->711 psia, then cleared.
anomalies.documented_cause: Air drawn into the manifold during launch-pad SHe servicing (manifold pressure dropped to zero because the purge shared the manifold regulator) condensed/froze in the tank heat exchanger, blocking it; blockage cleared ~35 s into the firing. GSE modified for Apollo 10. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Telemetry-detected; cause from ground testing.

anomalies.symptom: Supercritical helium tank pressure for the descent propulsion system decayed at 2.9 psi/hr immediately after the first descent firing shutdown and continued until staging (pressure should always rise under no-flow).
anomalies.documented_cause: ~0.1 lb/hr helium leak, probably a defective internal braze in the (internally-brazed, non-inspectable) supercritical-helium squib valve, most likely cracked by squib-firing shock. Apollo 10 uses externally brazed valve. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Telemetry-detected; cause from ground tests/analysis.

anomalies.symptom: The LM tracking light failed shortly after LM (ascent-stage) staging.
anomalies.documented_cause: Most likely a high-voltage breakdown in the pulse-forming network (other candidates: flash-head, HV cable, electronics package). Modified/arc-suppressed configurations qualified for Apollo 10/11. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Failure of the CSM-tracked LM light noted operationally (crew_initiated marked true with medium confidence); probable cause from failure-history analysis/testing, not in flight.

anomalies.symptom: The Lunar Module Pilot's push-to-talk switches (umbilical and attitude-control-assembly) were inoperative at ~89 hr; LMP used VOX for the remainder of LM operations.
anomalies.documented_cause: Probable discontinuity (broken wire) in the common wire to the parallel push-to-talk switches (failure of both switches improbable). Troubleshooting/backup-mode procedures added. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Crew worked around via VOX; probable cause from postflight analysis.

anomalies.symptom: During the third LM manning a caution-and-warning alarm occurred when the abort guidance system (AGS) was activated (no alarm on prior mannings).
anomalies.documented_cause: Most likely a shorted/broken wire between the abort electronics assembly and the signal-conditioner electronics assembly (or within those or the C&W assembly); AGS calibrated and temperature normal, ruling out real power/temperature limits. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Crew observed the C&W alarm; probable cause from analysis.

anomalies.symptom: When the LM forward hatch was opened for EVA it tended to bind on top and had to be pushed downward to open.
anomalies.documented_cause: Front-face insulation blankets around the hatch protruded below the fixed-structure shielding into the path of the hatch shield lip (clearances found reduced on the Apollo 10 LM; similar conditions inferred on Apollo 9). Hatch shield/trim redesign for Apollo 10+. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Crew reported; cause inferred from postflight inspection of the Apollo 10 LM.

anomalies.symptom: The LM forward hatch would not stay open during EVA.
anomalies.documented_cause: The door stop (snubber) intended to ride against floor Velcro could, under worst-case tolerances, leave a 0.040-inch clearance to the Velcro, so it failed to hold the door open. Redesigned snubber for Apollo 11+. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Crew reported; cause from tolerance analysis.

anomalies.symptom: Excessive cabin noise in the LM during helmets-off operation (one crewman improvised earpieces).
anomalies.documented_cause: Noise primarily from cabin fans, glycol pumps and suit compressors; glycol pumps couple acoustic energy into the glycol lines and pressure vessel (dominant). Single-fan procedure, earpieces, and later isolation mods. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Crew reported; sources identified by postflight noise measurements.

anomalies.symptom: Axial accelerometer data indicated that lateral loads at S-IC (first-stage) shutdown probably caused the LM descent-tank helium diffuser flange to contact the upper-deck sheet-metal flange.
anomalies.documented_cause: Lateral loads at S-IC shutdown caused a momentary structural contact; no detectable effect on any system or vehicle performance. Reduced loads predicted for Apollo 10. Closed for Apollo 10 (integrity evaluation continuing for Apollo 11+).
anomalies.notes: Detected via accelerometer/telemetry data, not by the crew.

anomalies.symptom: Pressing the DEDA CLEAR pushbutton frequently illuminated the operator-error light; four or five presses were often needed before it stayed out.
anomalies.documented_cause: One of the two CLEAR microswitches intermittently failed to actuate (suspected slightly bent switch leaf or small contamination), so the abort-electronics discrete that resets the shift discrete was not issued and the error light re-lit on release. Switch-jumper mod for Apollo 11+. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Crew reported repeatedly; cause from postflight teardown/analysis (no contamination actually found).

anomalies.symptom: During the second descent-engine firing the engine ran rough at about 27% throttle for a few seconds (oxidizer then fuel interface pressures rose, chamber pressure fluctuated), then smoothed out.
anomalies.documented_cause: Helium ingestion into the propellant lines (zero-g can uncovered plus lateral/rotational accelerations with ~60% ullage) caused cavitation/chamber-pressure fluctuations; matched ground tests with helium deliberately introduced. No detrimental effect. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Observed in firing data (and by crew); cause established by ground testing.

anomalies.symptom: At the start of the second ascent-engine firing the regulated helium pressure to the propellant tanks dropped from 186 to 176 psia (nominal 184) for most of the burn, then stepped up to ~179 psia at 290 s until oxidizer depletion.
anomalies.documented_cause: Most likely contamination of the class I primary helium regulator (restricting the feedback line or binding the main piston) so the class II regulator controlled; likelihood raised by backflow during a launch-site solenoid-valve replacement (no in-line filter). Assessment pending. Anomaly OPEN.
anomalies.notes: The only anomaly the report left OPEN pending detailed test-data review. Telemetry-detected.

anomalies.symptom: After the EVA the Lunar Module Pilot removed his liquid-cooled garment and found many air bubbles entrained in the liquid tubes.
anomalies.documented_cause: Air ingested through the sublimator into the coolant loop when the PLSS was connected to the LCG in the pressurized cabin (make-up line location draws air whenever LCG pressure is below PLSS pressure). PLSS make-up line relocated for Apollo 11. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Crew noted the bubbles; cause established by analysis/ground tests.

anomalies.symptom: When the crew tried to restow the oxygen purge system (OPS) pallet, the locking pin could not be inserted all the way through the LM bulkhead into the pallet.
anomalies.documented_cause: Bulkhead-bracket hole location plus adjacent-structure interference, poor lighting and an awkward insertion angle. Apollo 9 was the only mission using this pallet/location; OPS relocated and a ball-detent pin used on Apollo 10+. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Crew-encountered stowage difficulty; cause is a design/access issue.

anomalies.symptom: During docking, the sunlit command module background 'washed out' the reticle image of the LM crewman optical alignment sight (COAS).
anomalies.documented_cause: The COAS neutral-density filter (fitted for night star visibility) plus excessive specular reflection off the CM (vehicle/sun/earth geometry) drove the background above ~10,000 foot-lamberts, overwhelming the ~80 foot-lambert reticle. Diffuser glass + snap-on filter and docking-attitude changes for Apollo 10+. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Crew observed during docking; cause from photometric analysis.

anomalies.symptom: The checkout light on the Commander's oxygen purge system (OPS) operated erratically during the flight and failed to come on during rendezvous preparations.
anomalies.documented_cause: The main power switch actuator mechanism did not close the switch. Actuator changes (Teflon insert, swivel joint, increased cam rise, bonded cam/switch) for Apollo 10+. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Crew observed erratic/failed light; cause from postflight examination.

anomalies.symptom: The Commander reported one loss of communications while using the lightweight headset and one while using the communications carrier.
anomalies.documented_cause: Most probable cause a loose airlock sleeve on one of three connectors, or improper mating of the lightweight-headset connector to the suit harness/T-adapter (loose sleeves found postflight). Sleeves to be torqued and Loctited for Apollo 10+. Closed.
anomalies.notes: Crew reported; cause from postflight connector checks.

anomalies.symptom: When CM RCS system B propellant isolation valves were opened ~10 hr before launch, helium manifold pressure dropped from 44 to 37 psia, indicating a ruptured oxidizer burst disc.
anomalies.documented_cause: Oxidizer burst disc failed due to overpressure; postflight the oxidizer and fuel discs were similar in appearance confirming pressure failure. Redundant isolation valve allowed launch to proceed. CLOSED.
anomalies.notes: Report item 15.1.1. Detected on the ground prelaunch via manifold pressure; managed by procedure.

anomalies.symptom: CM RCS system A helium manifold pressure decayed ~0.13 psi/hr after servicing 3.5 days before launch, dropping from 45 to 37 psia.
anomalies.documented_cause: Slight leak in the low-pressure helium manifold on the fuel leg, at a rate acceptable for the mission; leak self-corrected as mission progressed. Postflight mass-spectrometer check found no leak. CLOSED.
anomalies.notes: Report item 15.1.2. Ground-detected prelaunch.

anomalies.symptom: At 98:51:54, following undocking, the CM rendezvous radar transponder would not operate; self-test read all zeros.
anomalies.documented_cause: CMP checked the circuit breaker and cycled the PWR-OFF-HEATER switch to OFF and back to PWR; transponder then worked for the rest of its use. Root cause left as an intermittent fault (SM wiring, power control box, transponder, or switch config); never conclusively isolated. CLOSED.
anomalies.notes: Report item 15.1.3. CREW-DIAGNOSED/self-restored in flight by switch cycling; no crew-report->CapCom-diagnosis air-to-ground exchange located within the 2-fetch budget, so turns=-1.

anomalies.symptom: Primary ECS evaporator started after lift-off but dried out after a few minutes; dried out again in second lunar orbit.
anomalies.documented_cause: Water-control microswitch actuator overtravel was marginal (as little as 0.0008 in beyond opening point); with environmental changes the switch would not always open to supply water. Found by postflight testing. Crew ran secondary cooling. CLOSED.
anomalies.notes: Report item 15.1.4.

anomalies.symptom: Twice during revolution 10, LM transmissions on VHF simplex-A were not received in the CM.
anomalies.documented_cause: Most probable cause: due to numerous switch-configuration changes in both vehicles, the two spacecraft were not configured simultaneously for simplex-A. Crew worked around using simplex-B; simplex-A worked later. CLOSED.
anomalies.notes: Report item 15.1.5. Crew noticed and worked around; probable cause from analysis.

anomalies.symptom: At 120:47, a short circuit in the AC pump package of fuel cell 1 tripped its circuit breaker; breaker could not be reset.
anomalies.documented_cause: Phase-to-phase short, most probably an insulation breakdown in the hydrogen pump stator (hot moist hydrogen degrades insulation); a basic design life-limit. Determined by circuit analysis and endurance-test history. Crew kept the cell operative by managing bus/skin temperature. CLOSED.
anomalies.notes: Report item 15.1.7. Detected via tripped breaker/telemetry.

anomalies.symptom: At 166:49, during a fuel-cell 1 hydrogen purge, hydrogen flow decayed abnormally slowly and regulated hydrogen pressure rose to 72 psia before returning to 62 psia.
anomalies.documented_cause: Extended cryogenic purge cooled the regulator below -10 F, causing seal leakage (continued flow); with the vent-line heater off the vent blocked, raising regulated pressure. Reproduced in tests. Extended purges banned for future flights. CLOSED.
anomalies.notes: Report item 15.1.8.

anomalies.symptom: During the fuel-cell 1 purge the hydrogen automatic pressure control appeared to fail twice to turn tank heaters off; crew switched heaters on/off manually after 170.5 hr.
anomalies.documented_cause: Hydrogen pressure transducers (temperature-compensated only to -20 F) were cold-soaked to -100 to -140 F during the extended purge and drifted upward, creating an apparent loss of automatic control. Determined by test. CLOSED.
anomalies.notes: Report item 15.1.9.

anomalies.symptom: Crew reported the gyro display coupler drifting excessively in roll and yaw (~5 deg in 20 min).
anomalies.documented_cause: Crew drove the GDC from both gyro assemblies and saw similar indications, isolating the drift to the gyro display coupler itself. Postflight bench tests could not reproduce the reported rate; possibly the divergence was not actually as rapid as it appeared. CLOSED.
anomalies.notes: Report item 15.1.10. CREW-DIAGNOSED: crew isolated cause to the GDC in flight. No timestamped crew-report->CapCom-diagnosis exchange sought/found; turns=-1.

anomalies.symptom: Data storage equipment lost data three times during entry (~33 s of PCM and 2 s of voice).
anomalies.documented_cause: An outside-to-inside pressure differential of ~2.25 psi deformed the recorder cover into the tape reels; the vent valve cracked at 2.40 psid (high side of spec). Found by postflight testing. CLOSED.
anomalies.notes: Report item 15.1.11.

anomalies.symptom: The entry-monitor stylus stopped scribing while the scroll was driven to the entry pattern; after slewing back and forth it began cutting through the emulsion.
anomalies.documented_cause: Scroll emulsion hardened due to a recent change in the commercially procured soap formulation (uric acid added), which reacted with the film. Determined postflight. Trace was still normal through entry. CLOSED.
anomalies.notes: Report item 15.1.12.

anomalies.symptom: The VHF recovery beacon antenna did not properly deploy (radiating element and three ground-plane radials).
anomalies.documented_cause: One radial was caught under the outboard edge of the ramp. Observed in recovery photographs postflight; RF signals were still received. CLOSED.
anomalies.notes: Report item 15.1.13.

anomalies.symptom: Crew reported gas in the ground-serviced potable water; fuel-cell water also contained hydrogen.
anomalies.documented_cause: Water serviced non-deaerated under nitrogen at ~20 psia releases gas when drawn into the 5-psia cabin; deaeration would not help (bladder re-saturates). A whirling separator bag flown did not work; a membrane device adopted for future flights. CLOSED.
anomalies.notes: Report item 15.1.14.

anomalies.symptom: The tunnel between the CM and LM could not be depressurized to ambient through the tunnel vent system.
anomalies.documented_cause: An incorrect fitting had been installed on the vent; the proper part was specified in procedures but the end-to-end verification test had been waived on Apollo 10. Found by postflight inspection. CLOSED.
anomalies.notes: Report item 15.1.16. Directly caused the later LM cabin-pressure drop at jettison (15.2.12).

anomalies.symptom: When the LM cabin was first pressurized, thermal coating on the CM forward (docking) hatch came off in pieces.
anomalies.documented_cause: Insulation-blanket vent holes were plugged (possibly by preflight 900 F bake weakening the insulation, or holes sealed by RTV/H-film tape), so tunnel depressurization damaged the coating. Insulation deleted for Apollo 11. CLOSED.
anomalies.notes: Report item 15.1.17.

anomalies.symptom: At 134 hr the crew reported fuel-cell 2 condenser exit temperature cycling 149-168 F at ~2 cycles/min, triggering the low-temperature caution/warning about every tenth cycle.
anomalies.documented_cause: Condenser-exit temperature disturbances excited oscillations under low radiator temperature (<80 F) and high current (two-fuel-cell operation forced by the fuel-cell 1 pump failure). Mechanism still under study. Non-detrimental nuisance. OPEN.
anomalies.notes: Report item 15.1.21. Listed as OPEN in the report.

anomalies.symptom: Recovery forces saw the flashing light operating on the main parachutes but not after landing.
anomalies.documented_cause: Postflight the glass tube containing the flashing element was found cracked; replacing the bulb assembly restored operation. Further analysis pending. OPEN; a separate Anomaly Report to be published.
anomalies.notes: Report item 15.1.23. Listed as OPEN.

anomalies.symptom: A master alarm and engine pitch gimbal fail warning were received during the descent-engine phasing maneuver.
anomalies.documented_cause: Gimbal 'coasting' (spring-loaded brake failing to engage after drive-signal removal) allowed ~0.25 s of uncommanded movement at a command reversal, tripping the fail logic; not detrimental and not unexpected (seen in checkout). Brake redesigned for Apollo 11. CLOSED.
anomalies.notes: Report item 15.2.1.

anomalies.symptom: Crew reported three master alarms during the descent-engine phasing maneuver, including a descent propellant low-quantity indication that cleared when the alarm was reset.
anomalies.documented_cause: A gas bubble uncovered/latched the low-level propellant sensor; plus a probable intermittent wire/electronics/connector fault (and intermittent tone) to match crew observations. Descent low-quantity alarm removed from master alarm for Apollo 11. CLOSED.
anomalies.notes: Report item 15.2.2.

anomalies.symptom: At the start of revolution 13 the LM S-band steerable antenna did not track; signal strength gradually fell ~20 dB over 13 min.
anomalies.documented_cause: Antenna was not moving; probable cause the track-mode switch was inadvertently left in SLEW or OFF instead of AUTO (crew reported the switch may have been mis-set). Antenna worked before and after. CLOSED.
anomalies.notes: Report item 15.2.4. Ground noticed the signal decay.

anomalies.symptom: Crew reported three optical anomalies with the LM alignment optical telescope: hair-like reticle contamination, a dimmer thumbwheel that fell forward, and stars disappearing ~6 star-diameters from reticle center.
anomalies.documented_cause: Reticle contamination via the redirectional-mirror air gap; the dimmer behavior is normal (mechanical cam override); star disappearance likely a contaminated prism surface (e.g. fingerprint smudge). Determined by analysis. CLOSED.
anomalies.notes: Report item 15.2.5 (AOT).

anomalies.symptom: Crew reported gas in the LM drinking water.
anomalies.documented_cause: Nitrogen used to pressurize the water permeates the bladder and saturates the water within ~100 hr; released as pressure drops. Unserviced hose/gun/plumbing added entrapped air. Prelaunch servicing changed. CLOSED.
anomalies.notes: Report item 15.2.6.

anomalies.symptom: The LM yaw rate gyro output differed from actual yaw rate for ~50 s before staging and several seconds after (erroneously indicating about -1.7 deg/s).
anomalies.documented_cause: Suspected stiction from contamination lodged in the 0.002-0.003 in float-to-case clearance (this gyro had a contamination/stiction rebuild history), cleared by the high rates after staging. Determined by analysis postflight; the report states the crew diagnosed the gyro problem in flight. CLOSED.
anomalies.notes: Report item 15.2.10. CREW-DIAGNOSED in flight. Report (15.2.14) states verbatim: 'The gyro problem was properly diagnosed by the crew after a number of hand controller operations.' This was a crew self-diagnosis during a dynamic staging event, not a crew-report->CapCom-diagnosis exchange; the migrated AFJ 'A surprise at staging' page did not render a timestamped transcript (grep found no GET timestamps/speaker lines), so turns=-1 per the hard rule. get_report/get_diagnosis unknown.

anomalies.symptom: Multiple LM instrumentation discrepancies: RCS chamber-pressure switches failing closed; glycol temperature reading zero on pump-2; RCS-A/B manifold pressure transducers dropping/reading low; cask thermal-shield temperature at upper limit; descent oxidizer tank ullage pressure reading zero on the cabin display.
anomalies.documented_cause: Various: particulate/propellant contamination holding pressure-switch diaphragms closed; broken jumper / bad contact in the pump-2 switch position; defective wiring splice or transducer calibration shift; broken wire / failed baroswitch on the cask measurement; transducer or wiring fault on descent oxidizer display. RCS performance unaffected. CLOSED.
anomalies.notes: Report item 15.2.11 (grouped instrumentation discrepancies).

anomalies.symptom: During LM ascent-stage jettison/separation from the CM, LM cabin pressure dropped rapidly from 4.86 psia to ~0.70 psia (measured by three transducers).
anomalies.documented_cause: Because the tunnel could not be vented (capped vent line, item 15.1.16), separation-pyro pressure loading exceeded the LM upper hatch latch capability; the hatch opened and reclosed within ~0.3 s, venting the cabin. Determined from motion pictures, telemetry, and static hatch pressure-to-failure test (latch failed at 4.1 psid). CLOSED.
anomalies.notes: Report item 15.2.12. Crew already back in the CM; telemetry/film-based diagnosis.

anomalies.symptom: Indicated LM cabin CO2 rose from 97-101 hr about 8x faster than predicted, then stayed constant for ~5 hr.
anomalies.documented_cause: Combination of lithium hydroxide cartridge performance variability (optimistic flight prediction) and CO2-sensor tolerance (+/-10% of full scale); no channeling or bypass found. Adequate for Apollo 11; more testing for longer missions. CLOSED.
anomalies.notes: Report item 15.2.13.

anomalies.symptom: Large LM attitude excursions before and during staging: body rates of 19 deg/s pitch and >25 deg/s roll and yaw; the AGS mode indication changed from ATT HOLD to AUTO with the vehicle 'wallowing' and gyrating.
anomalies.documented_cause: Concluded (postflight, by elimination of switches/connectors/wiring) to be inadvertent cycling of the abort-guidance mode-control switch to AUTO while the crew reacted to the erroneous yaw rate gyro output; AGS Z-axis steering then commanded the LM to point its Z-axis at the CM. Crew recovered manually in real time. CLOSED.
anomalies.notes: Report item 15.2.14. The famous LM staging gyrations. Crew recognized/recovered in flight but the documented root cause (inadvertent switch cycling) is a postflight conclusion, hence diagnosed_in_flight=false. No timestamped CapCom diagnostic exchange located; turns=-1.

anomalies.symptom: The ascent-propulsion low-propellant warning light came on ~1 s after the start of the first ascent-engine firing and triggered a master alarm; it went out ~1 s later.
anomalies.documented_cause: A gas bubble momentarily uncovered the (non-latching) oxidizer low-level sensor during the +X settling firing; valid indication. +X settling firing time to be increased. CLOSED.
anomalies.notes: Report item 15.2.15.

anomalies.symptom: During the low-altitude lunar pass the LM Hasselblad 70-mm camera stopped due to film binding in the magazine.
anomalies.documented_cause: Internal damage to the film-advance mechanism (burrs on the film guide) scraped emulsion onto the rollers, overloading the drive motor until it failed; the 1.6 A fuse protects against shorts but not continuous overload. Found postflight. CLOSED.
anomalies.notes: Report item 15.3.1 (GFE).

anomalies.symptom: During the low-altitude pass the LM 16-mm camera failed to operate with magazine F installed.
anomalies.documented_cause: Marginal clearances at the camera/magazine interface required greater care with magazine F; crew swapped in magazine G and the camera worked (magazine F worked later). Clearance-selection screening added. CLOSED.
anomalies.notes: Report item 15.3.2 (GFE). Crew worked around by swapping magazines; root cause found postflight.

anomalies.symptom: At ~173 hr (transearth coast) the CM 16-mm camera ceased operating in pulse mode.
anomalies.documented_cause: The magazine interlock microswitch failed due to internal contamination and a faulty plunger (a non-high-reliability item). High-reliability microswitches installed for Apollo 11. CLOSED.
anomalies.notes: Report item 15.3.3 (GFE).

anomalies.symptom: During the lunar orbit insertion firing, gaseous nitrogen in the redundant service propulsion engine actuation system decayed from 2307 to 1883 psia, indicating a leak downstream of the injector prevalve; no performance degradation, one system only.
anomalies.documented_cause: Contamination-induced failure of a solenoid control valve; suspected source a contaminated vendor facility manifold. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Telemetry-detected during LOI; integral filters added on Apollo 12+.

anomalies.symptom: Automatic pressure control data showed one of the two heater elements in cryogenic oxygen tank 2 was inoperative; detected in launch-countdown current readings.
anomalies.documented_cause: Probable intermittent contact on a 16-gauge terminal board in the heater circuit; redundant heater so no mission constraint. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Cryogenic oxygen (fuel-cell/ECS) tank heater. Not reported to proper channels preflight because no spec limits were in the test procedure.

anomalies.symptom: Minus-yaw engine in command module reaction control system 1 produced low and erratic thrust when fired through the automatic coils; normal on direct coils.
anomalies.documented_cause: Two loose pins in the engine-valve terminal board caused intermittent continuity to the automatic coils; improper clip position relative to bus-bar counterbore. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Verified by spacecraft rates; root cause found in postflight tests.

anomalies.symptom: An electroluminescent segment on the entry monitor system velocity counter numeric display would not illuminate.
anomalies.documented_cause: Misrouting of logic wires across terminal strips with sharp ends puncturing insulation, causing shorts (consistent with prior similar cases). Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Crew-observed display fault; cause established postflight, no in-flight diagnosis exchange.

anomalies.symptom: During initial lunar-module pressurization, two master alarms were activated as the oxygen flow rate was decreasing from full scale.
anomalies.documented_cause: Open EMI-filter (metalized Mylar) capacitor in the oxygen flow sensing circuit allowed relay K1 chatter that timed out a false master alarm. Nuisance only. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Same condition seen in altitude-chamber tests preflight; duplicated postflight.

anomalies.symptom: The propellant isolation valves on quad B of the service module RCS closed during CSM/S-IVB separation.
anomalies.documented_cause: Separation shock closed the magnetically latched valves (similar to Apollo 9); crew checklist already contained precautionary reopen guidance. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Indication/telemetry event.

anomalies.symptom: An odor similar to burned wire insulation was detected in the docking tunnel when the hatch was first opened; no discoloration or overheating found.
anomalies.documented_cause: Outgassing of the docking-hatch ablator (higher ablator temperatures after removal of outer TG-15000 insulation). Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Crew investigated circuits in flight; odor source identified by postflight comparison samples.

anomalies.symptom: Shortly after launch the oxygen flow-rate indication read at the lower instrumentation limit rather than the nominal metabolic rate.
anomalies.documented_cause: Instrumentation bias (~1.5 lb/hr) from an increase in heater-winding resistance (1000 to 1600 ohms) in the flow-sensor bridge; actual flow normal. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Instrumentation-only; confirmed by postflight transducer tests.

anomalies.symptom: Postflight examination found all but one tie-wrap knot untied on the forward heat shield mortar umbilical lanyard.
anomalies.documented_cause: Installation error: a clove hitch used instead of two half-hitches; could untie and lengthen the lanyard, risking premature disconnect of the forward heat shield mortar umbilical. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Purely postflight finding on CM 107 (and SC 110/111).

anomalies.symptom: During lunar orbit operations the glycol temperature control valve did not control evaporator inlet temperature; early temperature rise then evaporator outlet dropped to 31 F on revolution 15.
anomalies.documented_cause: A bearing retainer in the valve gear train disengaged from its race and interfered with worm-gear travel; high stall thrust loads exceeded the bearing rating. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Anomaly cleared when crew cycled the glycol evaporator temp inlet switch; root cause found by postflight valve teardown.

anomalies.symptom: After jettison the service module did not skip out as designed; C-band tracking showed low separation velocity, the crew sighted it ~5 minutes later, and aircraft photos showed it entering and disintegrating near the command module.
anomalies.documented_cause: Propellant sloshing driven by tip-off/precession made the SM unstable, reducing net separation velocity (also seen on Apollo 8 and 10); jettison controller timing revised for Apollo 13+. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Trajectory/design anomaly analyzed postflight; crew sighting noted but not a diagnosis.

anomalies.symptom: The crew reported shortly after lunar landing that the mission timer had stopped and could not be restarted; power was removed to let it cool and it was restarted ~11 hours later.
anomalies.documented_cause: Most probable cause a cracked solder joint from cordwood construction (differential expansion of potting compound); cooling let the joint remake contact. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Crew reported and empirically worked around (power off to cool); root cause was a postflight probable-cause conclusion, not an in-flight ground diagnosis.

anomalies.symptom: During simultaneous venting of descent propellant and supercritical helium tanks, fuel froze in the fuel/helium heat exchanger and post-landing engine heat soakback raised trapped-line pressure into an out-of-range regime.
anomalies.documented_cause: Fuel frozen in the heat exchanger then thermally expanded by descent-engine heat soakback; line pressure likely 700-800 psia; heat exchanger thawed in ~0.5 hr and pressure decayed harmlessly. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Telemetry-monitored DPS pressure; interface transducer range 0-300 psia so value inferred. Procedure change (close solenoid valve before fuel vent) for later missions.

anomalies.symptom: Shortly after lunar module ascent the crew reported the carbon dioxide partial pressure indication was high and erratic; switching LiOH canisters had no effect and a caution/warning alarm activated.
anomalies.documented_cause: Free water reached the optical section of the CO2 sensor (condensate from the drain tank leaking up the vent line), disturbing the light-transmission measurement. Anomaly closed; vent line relocated on Apollo 13.
anomalies.notes: Crew reported and tried canister swap; root cause established postflight.

anomalies.symptom: When the steerable (S-band) antenna was selected after acquisition on revolution 14, down-link signal strength was lower than predicted and repeatedly dropped to loss-of-lock.
anomalies.documented_cause: Antenna pointed into/near vehicle-blockage regions plus multipath from the lunar surface; the Spacecraft Operational Data Book coverage diagram was in error and omitted the added thruster plume deflectors. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Comm-performance anomaly; antenna hardware operated properly. Cause analyzed postflight.

anomalies.symptom: Five computer (guidance) program alarms of the Executive-overflow type (1202, then a 1201) occurred during powered descent prior to low gate; guidance and control performance was not affected.
anomalies.documented_cause: Rendezvous-radar coupling-data-unit counter interrupts (from a phase mismatch between two 800-Hz references) usurped >10-15% of computer time, causing multiple scheduling of the same job and software restarts; the AGC priority design protected critical guidance jobs. Anomaly closed; Luminary 1B ignores those interrupts.
anomalies.exchange_quote: 102:38:26 Armstrong: 'Program Alarm.' / 102:38:30 Armstrong: 'It's a 1202.' / 102:38:32 Aldrin: '1202.' / 102:38:48 Armstrong: 'Give us a reading on the 1202 program alarm.' / 102:38:53 Duke (CapCom): 'Roger. We got you... we're go on that alarm.'
anomalies.notes: THE crew-report -> real-time ground-diagnosis anomaly. Steve Bales (GUIDO) and backroom Jack Garman assessed the AGC and passed a GO via CapCom Charlie Duke. Turn count counts the crew's alarm report/reading-request downlink and CapCom's GO uplink as the diagnostic exchange (~27 s from first callout at 102:38:26 to GO at 102:38:53). Timestamps corroborated across NASA transcript, ALSJ program-alarms page, and RMG; exact integer turn count is a judgment (2).

anomalies.symptom: Decompression of the cabin prior to extravehicular activity took longer than anticipated (~5 minutes).
anomalies.documented_cause: Flow restriction of the bacteria filter in the vent path; removing it on Apollo 12+ cut decompression time to under 2 minutes. Crew could not damage the hatch by opening prematurely. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Crew-experienced ECLSS/EVA egress issue; assessed postflight.

anomalies.symptom: An electroluminescent segment on the abort guidance system data entry and display assembly (DEDA) numeric display was reported inoperative, making 3 and 9 hard to distinguish.
anomalies.documented_cause: Analogous delta-qual failure traced to a faulty epoxy process producing a cracked/open electrode in the light-emitting element; no generic-problem history. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Crew-reported display fault (AGS/DEDA); cause from analysis, no in-flight diagnosis exchange.

anomalies.symptom: Voice-operated relay operation during EVA caused breakup of voice received by the Manned Space Flight Network, primarily from the Lunar Module Pilot.
anomalies.documented_cause: Most probable cause an inadvertent low setting of the Commander's LM VOX sensitivity control (should have been maximum per checklist); not an inherent design problem. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Ground-observed (MSFN) comm quality issue during EVA; cause from ground tests.

anomalies.symptom: A voice turnaround (echo) was heard during EVA while the lunar module operated in relay mode.
anomalies.documented_cause: Acoustical/mechanical coupling between the communications-carrier earphone and microphone re-keyed the relay; inherent to the comm-carrier design. Mitigated by inhibiting down-link remoting during up-link voice. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Duplicated in the laboratory; EVA comm relay path.

anomalies.symptom: The data storage electronics assembly (onboard recorder) did not record properly; postflight playback showed low, noisy voice with a 400-Hz tone and missing timing-code switching.
anomalies.documented_cause: Most probable cause two broken 26-gauge wires in the vehicle harness to the recorder (similar breaks found in LTA-8); harness protection added on later vehicles. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Discovered on postflight tape playback; instrumentation/recorder.

anomalies.symptom: The crew reported after EVA that the knob on the engine-arm circuit breaker was broken (and two other breakers were closed); the breaker was still successfully closed for ascent.
anomalies.documented_cause: Probable impact of the oxygen purge system (aft edge) against the circuit breaker during EVA preparation; breaker guards added on Apollo 12+. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Famous 'broken engine-arm breaker' repaired by crew with a marker; report attributes damage to OPS impact (postflight).

anomalies.symptom: The chamber pressure switch monitoring the quad 2 aft-firing ascent-stage engine (A2A) showed slow response and failed to respond to seven consecutive minimum-impulse commands just before terminal phase initiation, giving a master alarm and thruster warning flag that the crew reset.
anomalies.documented_cause: Most probable cause particulate contamination in the switch inlet passage, reducing chamber-gas flow and slowing switch closing response; engine itself operated normally. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Crew reset the alarm/flag but did not troubleshoot; cause determined postflight.

anomalies.symptom: After the lunar module reached orbit, water (about a tablespoon) began entering the Commander's suit in spurts at ~1-minute intervals through the suit half-vent duct.
anomalies.documented_cause: Most probable source leakage through the water-separator selector valve (misalignment/binding), letting free water pass the idle separator into the suit hose. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Crew self-resolved empirically by selecting the secondary water separator (spurts stopped); root cause was a postflight most-probable-source conclusion, no air-to-ground diagnosis exchange, so -1.

anomalies.symptom: The crew reported thrust chamber assembly warning flags for three engine pairs (quads 2 and 4 system A simultaneously, then quad 4 system B) during LM station keeping and before powered descent initiation, believed accompanied by master alarms.
anomalies.documented_cause: Most likely a single-point failure (momentary loss of +28 V dc or oscillator to a 10-buffer module in the signal conditioner electronics) that cleared itself; sufficient data not available to confirm. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Crew reported and reset flags; cause uncertain, established (tentatively) postflight.

anomalies.symptom: The lunar-surface television camera cable retained its coiled shape after deployment, creating loops that were a tripping hazard to the crew.
anomalies.documented_cause: Cable memory of coiled stowage; investigated material/stowage changes gave only minimal improvement at a weight penalty, so no hardware change made. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Government-furnished equipment (TV camera cable); observed on surface.

anomalies.symptom: During EVA preparation the crew had considerable difficulty mating the electrical connectors from the remote control unit to the portable life support system.
anomalies.documented_cause: The coupling lock ring rotated freely on the connector shell, preventing rotational polarization alignment; connector redesigned (positive-position lock ring, conical-tipped pins) for later missions. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: GFE crew-interface anomaly; cause understood from hardware.

anomalies.symptom: The force required to close the sample return containers was much higher than expected, made worse by an unstable work table and inadequate retention.
anomalies.documented_cause: Contractor cleaning procedure removed all lubricant from the latch linkage (raising closing force up to ~24 lb) and the flight container had not been exercised like the training unit; burnishing lubricant after cleaning incorporated. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: GFE (sample return containers); crew-experienced, cause from ground tests.

anomalies.symptom: During the first minute of flight the vehicle was struck by two triggered lightning discharges (36.5 s and 52 s). Crew got master alarms, multiple caution/warning lights (three fuel-cell lights, AC bus light, fuel-cell disconnect, AC bus overload 1 and 2, Main Bus A and B out), a signal-conditioning-equipment (SCE) dropout that garbled telemetry, and loss/tumble of the inertial guidance platform.
anomalies.documented_cause: Vehicle-triggered lightning as it passed through electric fields (special report, ref. 12). First strike's induced transient on the battery-relay bus exceeded the current rate-of-change limit of the SCRs in the fuel-cell overload sensors, disconnecting the fuel cells from the main buses; low bus voltage dropped out the SCE and tripped AC undervoltage. Second strike set high-order bits in the CDU, driving the Z-axis (yaw) middle-gimbal readout past 85 deg and down-moding the platform to coarse-align, causing the observed tumble. Nine SM instrumentation measurements permanently lost. Crew restored fuel-cell power to buses at 000:02:22. Anomaly closed; launch weather rules added for later missions.
anomalies.exchange_quote: Air-to-ground (radio) turns, crew report -> CapCom diagnosis (Apollo Flight Journal, Day 1 pt 1; 2nd strike/platform loss at 000:00:52): (1) Conrad: 'Okay, we just lost the platform, gang. I don't know what happened here; we had everything in the world drop out.' (2) Carr: 'Roger. Plus one.' (3) Conrad: 'I got three fuel cell lights, an AC bus light, a fuel cell disconnect, AC bus overload 1 and 2, Main Bus A and B out.' (4, diagnosis) 000:01:36 Carr: 'Apollo 12, Houston. Try SCE to auxiliary. Over.' [reaffirmed 000:01:43 Carr: 'SCE, SCE to auxiliary.'] Tightly-timestamped context: 000:01:33 Conrad (onboard): 'We've got a short on it of some kind...'; 000:01:36 Carr: 'Try SCE to auxiliary.'
anomalies.notes: THE marquee anomaly; the only one turn-hunted. John Aaron (EECOM) recognized the garbled-telemetry pattern and called 'SCE to Auxiliary'; Bean threw the SCE switch and telemetry was restored. Counted 4 air-to-ground turns (2 strictly intervening) from Conrad's report of the electrical emergency to Carr's diagnosis. get_report anchored to AFJ-documented 000:00:52 second strike / platform loss (Conrad's downlinked report immediately followed, not separately inline-timestamped); get_diagnosis 000:01:36 is inline in the transcript; human_time_s=44 is therefore approximate to a few seconds. Report Section 14.1.3 'Electrical Potential Discharges'.

anomalies.symptom: Approximately 1.5 hours before launch the crew reported several intermittent all-8's displays on the command module main display and keyboard assembly (DSKY). No display malfunction occurred in flight.
anomalies.documented_cause: A short across the normally-closed contacts of any one relay in the display relay matrix applies 250 V ac to all segments (common discharge path). Failure analyses after four previous identical failures showed relay contamination as the likely cause. Fabrication moved to laminar-flow clean rooms, 100% vibration screening added, and a malfunction procedure devised to clear a shorted condition. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Report Section 14.1.1. Preflight crew report; cause from prior failure-analysis history, not an in-flight diagnosis.

anomalies.symptom: During cryogenic loading about 51 hours before launch, the heat leak of hydrogen tank 2 was unacceptable; a thick frost layer on the tank exterior verified inadequate vacuum in the insulating annulus. Tank removed and replaced before launch.
anomalies.documented_cause: Incomplete bond in the stainless-steel/titanium bimetallic joint let hydrogen leak from the inner tank into the vacuum annulus. Improper manufacturing inspection (lot 3B; lot 3A suspect) allowed voids to pass. Remaining suspect tanks recalled for joint replacement. Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Report Section 14.1.2. Ground/prelaunch cryo-loading anomaly, detected by ground data and visual frost check.

anomalies.symptom: During systems checks after earth-orbit insertion, stabilization-and-control circuit breaker 23 (logic buses 3 and 4, panel 8) was found open. A crewman closed it and it stayed closed for the rest of the mission.
anomalies.documented_cause: Postflight electrical and mechanical tests of the breaker and circuitry were normal; no cause found for launch-vibration or electrical-fault opening. Because it was fed in parallel with two breakers that did not open and showed no abnormalities, the breaker was probably not properly set during prelaunch positioning checks (these breakers are not specifically verified). Anomaly closed.
anomalies.notes: Report Section 14.1.4. Crew found and reclosed it; root cause not determined in flight (postflight conclusion).

anomalies.symptom: The crew reported that two RCS isolation valves (quad A secondary propellant isolation valve and quad B No. 1 helium isolation valve) had inadvertently closed during CSM/S-IVB separation. Crew reopened them per preplanned procedure with no further problems.
anomalies.documented_cause: Same shock-induced closure phenomenon seen on Apollo 9 and 11 for propellant isolation valves; the helium isolation valve closure was the first noted in-flight occurrence. Failure-investigation test programs (postflight). Crew recovery was procedural.
anomalies.notes: Report Section 14.1.5. Crew-reported; recovery procedural, root-cause investigation postflight.

anomalies.symptom: Operation of the S-band high-gain antenna in narrow-beam mode produced ~10-12 dB decreases in both uplink and downlink signal strength on several occasions; first observed in lunar-orbit revolution 1.
anomalies.documented_cause: Documented in Section 14.1.6 as unexpected narrow-beam signal-strength variations (analysis of antenna performance; details in Section 14.1.6).
anomalies.notes: Report Section 14.1.6. Ground/telemetry-observed signal-strength anomaly; detailed root cause not fully extracted.

anomalies.symptom: At end of mission a discrepancy of ~27 pounds of oxygen existed between measured total cryogenic oxygen usage and the calculated combined environmental-control-system + fuel-cell oxygen usage.
anomalies.documented_cause: Cryogenic O2 quantity-accounting discrepancy (Section 14.1.7); fuel-cell O2 usage calculated from produced current and cross-checked against hydrogen consumption. Detailed conclusion not fully extracted.
anomalies.notes: Report Section 14.1.7. Postflight accounting/telemetry discrepancy, not crew-detected in flight.

anomalies.symptom: The hatch, left-hand, and both rendezvous windows of the command module showed considerable contamination as vertical streaks on the exterior surfaces. Crew reported seeing water on the windows during heavy pre-launch rain and water flowing over the windows at tower jettison.
anomalies.documented_cause: Gaps in the boost protective cover (hard-to-soft transition over the left rendezvous window) were not sealed with the required sealant on final installation; rain/water intrusion deposited contamination that streaked the windows. Identified via prelaunch notes and postflight inspection.
anomalies.notes: Report Section 14.1.11. Crew observed water in flight; root cause (unsealed BPC gaps) confirmed on the ground.

anomalies.symptom: During ascent and rendezvous there was a VHF communications problem between the command module and lunar module; only one problem was apparent at the time but there were actually two separate problems. From ~142-1/4 hours, LM-to-CM comm had to be relayed via S-band network.
anomalies.documented_cause: Two separate VHF problems in the CM VHF configuration (LM-aft/CM-right antennas), analyzed postflight (Section 14.1.19).
anomalies.notes: Report Section 14.1.19. Crew experienced degraded VHF in flight; two-fault breakdown established postflight.

anomalies.symptom: After initial in-flight LM checkout, CSM-to-LM electrical current was ~1 ampere higher than expected. Turning off the docking-hatch floodlight circuit breaker returned current to normal.
anomalies.documented_cause: The docking-hatch floodlight is controlled by a plunger switch actuated by closing the hatch (like a refrigerator door). The hatch did not depress the plunger sufficiently to open the switch, so the floodlight stayed powered. Crew verified switch/floodlight operation by manually depressing the plunger.
anomalies.notes: Report Section 14.2.1 (LM). Detected via higher-than-expected bus current (telemetry/electrical), then isolated by the crew.

anomalies.symptom: During preparations for the first EVA, water came from both suit inlet hoses when disconnected. After EVA-1 the Commander reported water in his boots and cold moist air from the suit inlet hose; the LM Pilot noted water drops in his inlet hose.
anomalies.documented_cause: Free water in the suit loop; swapping the water separators gave no improvement. Water dried in the suit before the sleep period with no further problem. Managed operationally in flight (Section 14.2.2).
anomalies.notes: Report Section 14.2.2 (LM ECS). Crew-reported; handled operationally, no in-flight root-cause fix.

anomalies.symptom: Following lunar lift-off the crew reported a master alarm near ascent-engine shutdown; on a later pass behind the Moon the CO2 high-partial-pressure light and master alarm tripped again. Crew selected the secondary LiOH canister, then reselected primary at ground request; erratic CO2 indications continued on either canister.
anomalies.documented_cause: Erratic/faulty carbon-dioxide sensor: ground data showed only a short-duration spike in indicated CO2 partial pressure (i.e., not a real CO2 buildup); indications were erratic regardless of which LiOH canister was in use (Section 14.2.3).
anomalies.notes: Report Section 14.2.3 (LM). Crew-reported and treated in flight as an erratic sensor (ground had them reselect the primary canister), so it qualifies as crew-initiated + diagnosed-in-flight, but the specific air-to-ground exchange was NOT turn-hunted (fetch budget was spent on 14.1.3). Left at -1 per bounded-search rule.

anomalies.symptom: At the start of the second darkness pass after lunar lift-off, the crew reported the rendezvous tracking light had failed.
anomalies.documented_cause: Subsequent switch cycling showed normal power consumption, indicating a corona failure in the high-voltage section of the light. Same failure signature as Apollo 9 and ground testing (previously attributed to high-voltage corona); design modifications had been made after Apollo 9 (Section 14.2.4).
anomalies.notes: Report Section 14.2.4 (LM). Crew-reported; corona-failure conclusion drew on Apollo 9 comparison/analysis (treated as postflight diagnosis).

anomalies.symptom: During initial egress the Commander could not release the modularized equipment stowage assembly (MESA) D-ring deploy handle from its support bracket; it could be rotated but not pulled free. The compartment was deployed by pulling directly on the bellcrank cable.
anomalies.documented_cause: A retention pin at the bottom of the D-ring plugs into a socket with a ball-detent mechanism; apparently either the ball detent bound or the crewman did not fully release it (Section 14.2.5).
anomalies.notes: Report Section 14.2.5 (LM/EVA). Crew-experienced mechanical difficulty; cause analyzed on the ground.

anomalies.symptom: During egress the Commander's portable life support system (PLSS) contacted and tore the forward-hatch micrometeoroid/thermal shield, a potential hazard to the suit.
anomalies.documented_cause: Physical contact between the bulky PLSS and the thin hatch thermal shield during egress. For Apollo 13 and later, shield thickness increased (0.004->0.010 in general area; 0.020->0.040 in standoff) and mounting-hole diameter increased (0.375->0.5 in) to strengthen it (Section 14.2.6).
anomalies.notes: Report Section 14.2.6 (LM/EVA). Damage occurred/observed during egress; fix was a postflight redesign.

anomalies.symptom: The descent-propulsion low-level propellant quantity light illuminated about 20+ seconds earlier than expected during powered descent.
